# Function, option and example index {#sec-reference}

<!-- Generated by tools/make-reference.R from the pinned build. Do not edit by hand. -->

This chapter lists every ferx-r function, setting, model file block, data column, bundled example, warning category and fit object slot in the pinned build ({{< var ferx_r_sha_short >}}), with the chapter that covers it. It is generated from the book's feature inventory, the package's help pages and the ferx-core documentation of the pinned engine.

## Newer than ferx-r 0.4.0 {#sec-reference-newer}

ferx-r 0.4.0 is the last release. The pinned build is newer, and these 67 entries are not in 0.4.0 (for a fit slot: not on the result of 0.4.0's `ferx_fit()`). Each chapter that uses one says so in a callout. Behaviour that changed after 0.4.0 without a new name is marked where the book relies on it.

## Fit settings

Keys for `ferx_fit(settings = list(...))` and the `[fit_options]` block. The chapter column points at the section that uses the key; the ferx-core [fit options](https://ferx-nlme.org/ferx-core/model-file/fit-options.html) page gives the full semantics. A blank *Values* cell means the key takes a free value (a number, a name or a list) rather than a fixed set; a blank *Meaning* means the pinned engine documents the key only in terms of other software, which this book does not quote.

| Setting | Values | Default | Meaning | Chapter |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `accept` |  |  | Character vector of filter expressions. A record is kept only when all conditions pass; excluded if any fail. | @sec-data |
| `adapt_interval` |  | `50` | Iterations between step-size adaptation, under `scale_adaptation = interval`. | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `agq_eval_only` |  |  | (default FALSE) "laplace" only: TRUE evaluates -2 log L by adaptive quadrature at the incoming parameters instead of estimating, and must be the last stage of the chain -- the deterministic counterpart of imp_eval_only. | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `analytic_cov_hessian` | `true`, `false` | `true` | Use the **exact analytic R-matrix** for the covariance step when the model is in scope, instead of the finite-difference-of-OFV Hessian. | @sec-uncertainty |
| `bayes_chains` |  |  | Number of independent chains (default 4); used for split-R-hat. | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `bayes_iters` |  |  | Retained sampling sweeps per chain, before thinning (default 1000). | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `bayes_seed` |  |  | Base RNG seed for the Bayes sampler. Independent of seed / saem_seed. | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `bayes_thin` |  |  | Keep every bayes_thin-th sampling draw (default 1). | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `bayes_warmup` |  |  | Warmup (burn-in + adaptation) sweeps per chain, discarded from the posterior (default 1000). | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `checkpoint` | `true`, `false` | `true` | Periodically save a resume point so a run that is interrupted (e.g. `Ctrl-C`, a crashed job) can be restarted from where it stopped instead of from scratch. | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `checkpoint_interval_secs` | integer | `300` | Minimum wall-clock seconds between checkpoint writes. Larger values reduce I/O overhead but lose more progress on an interrupt; smaller values save more often. | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `conddist` |  | `false` | Run a post-fit conditional-distribution pass estimating each subject's `p(η_i \| y_i)` by MCMC. | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `conddist_burnin` |  | `20` | Burn-in draws discarded before accumulation, to forget the EBE-mode warm start. | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `conddist_keep_samples` |  | `false` | Retain the raw per-subject draws (written to `{model}-conddist-samples.csv`), not just the mean/SD. | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `conddist_nsamp` |  | `200` | Retained MCMC draws per subject in the conditional-distribution pass. | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `cov_inner_tol` | float | `inner_tol` (LTBS: `min(inner_tol, 1e-8)`) | Inner EBE-reconvergence tolerance used **only by the covariance step**, decoupled from `inner_tol`. | @sec-uncertainty |
| `covariance_fallback` | `none`, `sir` | `none` | What to do when the covariance Hessian is non-PD, whether `R` is analytic or finite-difference. | @sec-uncertainty |
| `covariance_method` | `r`, `s`, `rsr` | `r` | The estimator that produced cov_matrix and the standard errors: "r", "s" or "rsr", the [fit_options] token (ferx-core #1382). | @sec-uncertainty |
| `ebe_warm_start` |  | `false` | When an inner per-subject EBE solve fails its BFGS step and falls back to Nelder–Mead, warm-start the simplex from the BFGS partial η̂ rather than cold-starting from the prior mode η=0. | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `fd_hessian_step` | float | `1e-2` | Initial relative step size for the finite-difference Hessian used in the covariance step. | @sec-uncertainty |
| `frem_predictions` |  |  |  | @sec-covariates |
| `frem_rao_blackwell` |  | `true` | FREM only: Rao-Blackwellise the covariate ETAs (integrate them analytically, importance-sample only the PK ETAs). | @sec-covariates |
| `frem_sigma` |  |  |  | @sec-covariates |
| `global_maxeval` | integer | `0` (auto: `30 * (n_params + 1)`) | Maximum evaluations of the FOCE objective during the global pre-search. | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `global_search` | `true`, `false` | `false` | Run NLopt CRS2-LM (Controlled Random Search with Local Mutation) as a gradient-free global pre-search before the local optimizer. | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `gn_lambda` |  |  | Levenberg-Marquardt damping factor (default 0.01). Larger values make steps more conservative. | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `ignore` |  |  | Character vector of filter expressions that exclude a record when the expression evaluates to true. | @sec-data |
| `ignore_subjects` |  |  |  | @sec-data |
| `imp_auto` |  | `true` | Adaptive sample count. When `true`, `imp_samples` is the *starting* count and is ramped up (×2/iteration, cap 10000) while the objective's Monte-Carlo SE exceeds 1.0. | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `imp_averaging` |  | `50` | Terminal iterations averaged into the reported estimate (estimator only). | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `imp_defensive_alpha` |  | `0.0` | Defensive-mixture weight (issue #528), **opt-in**. Each subject draws this fraction of its samples from the prior `N(0, Ω)` rather than the mode-centred proposal, and every sample is scored under the mixture density. | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `imp_eval_only` |  | `false` | `true` ⇒ evaluate `−2 log L` at fixed parameters; must be the terminal chain stage. | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `imp_iterations` |  | `200` | MCEM iterations (estimator only). | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `imp_low_ess_threshold` |  | `0.1` | Subjects with normalized ESS below this fraction get flagged in the result. | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `imp_proposal_df` |  | `5.0` | Student-t proposal degrees of freedom (≥ 1), or `normal`/`mvn` for a multivariate-normal proposal. | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `imp_samples` |  | `1000` | Importance samples K per subject. 2000–5000 recommended for publication-quality MC SE. | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `imp_seed` |  | `12345` | RNG seed. Same seed → identical result. | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `imp_sobol` |  | `false` | Estimator only: Sobol quasi-random IS draws for the MCEM E-step, the `imp` counterpart of `impmap_sobol`. | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `impmap_auto` |  | `true` | Adaptive sample count. When `true`, `impmap_samples` is the *starting* count and is ramped up (×2/iteration, cap 10000) while the objective's Monte-Carlo SE exceeds 1.0. | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `impmap_averaging` |  | `50` | Final iterations whose parameters are averaged into the reported estimate (Monte-Carlo variance reduction). | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `impmap_iterations` |  | `200` | Number of MCEM iterations (parameter updates). | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `impmap_low_ess_threshold` |  | `0.1` | Subjects with normalized ESS below this fraction are flagged as poorly sampled. | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `impmap_mceta` |  | `0` | Number of additional random starting points for per-subject MAP optimization. | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `impmap_proposal_df` |  | `4` | Proposal degrees of freedom. A finite value ≥ 1 gives a heavier-tailed Student-t (default `4`); `normal` (or `mvn`) gives a multivariate-normal proposal. | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `impmap_samples` |  | `300` | Importance samples K per subject per iteration. Larger K reduces Monte-Carlo noise at linear cost. | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `impmap_seed` |  | `12345` | RNG seed. Same seed → identical estimates. | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `impmap_sobol` |  | `false` | Build each IS draw from an Owen-scrambled Sobol quasi-random point instead of pseudo-random numbers — the normals, the Student-t scale and the defensive-mixture component alike, so it applies to every proposal form. | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `impmap_trace` |  | `false` | Logical; when TRUE, collect per-iteration parameter values into fit$impmap_trace. | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `inits_from_nca` | `true`, `false`, `nca`, `nca_sweep`, `nca_ebe` | `false` | Derive NCA-based starting values from the data before the optimizer loop. | @sec-first-fit |
| `inner_maxiter` | integer | `200` | Max iterations for the inner (per-subject EBE) optimizer | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `inner_optimizer` | `auto`, `bfgs`, `lbfgs`, `nelder_mead` | `auto` | Inner-loop (per-subject EBE) optimisation algorithm. `auto` uses dense BFGS, switching to limited-memory L-BFGS above 32 random effects. | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `inner_restarts` | integer | `1` | Guarded multi-start count for the inner (per-subject EBE) optimizer, to escape a **multimodal individual objective**. | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `inner_screen` | integer ≥ 0 | `100` | Size `N` of the Sobol screen the cold multi-start runs before its per-coordinate seeds, to find an individual mode that lies off every axis (the flip-flop `ka ↔ CL/V` twin). | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `inner_tol` | float | `1e-5` | Gradient-norm convergence tolerance for the inner (per-subject EBE) optimizer. | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `inner_twin_seed` | `true`, `false` | `true` | Seed the cold multi-start with the subject's flip-flop twin before the screen: on a closed-form `one_cpt_oral` model whose `V` and `KA` are each log-normal on a random effect of their own, one descent from `η_V`, `η_KA` moved together by `ln(k/ka)`. | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `iov_column` | string | — | Name of the occasion column in the dataset (e.g. `OCC`). Supplies occasions when the model uses `kappa` or `block_kappa` declarations. | @sec-variability |
| `iov_occasion` | `column`, `dose`, `time(t₁, …)` | `column` | Derive the IOV occasion partition from the model instead of a data column. | @sec-variability |
| `iscale_max` |  | `10.0` | Maximum proposal scaling factor. | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `iscale_min` |  | `0.1` | Minimum proposal scaling factor for adaptive IS. The IS proposal covariance is multiplied by `s²` where `s` is chosen from `[iscale_min, iscale_max]` to maximise per-subject ESS. | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `max_unconverged_frac` |  | `0.1` | Fraction of subjects (with at least `min_obs_for_convergence_check` observations) allowed to have unconverged EBEs before the outer optimizer rejects the step. | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `maxiter` | integer | `500` | Maximum outer loop iterations. `maxiter = 0` is *evaluation only*: the engine runs one inner EBE solve at the initial parameters and reports the objective there with no outer optimisation — useful for scoring a fixed parameter set or computing standard errors at known estimates (with `covariance = true`). | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `min_obs_for_convergence_check` |  | `2` | Subjects with fewer than this many observations are excluded from the `max_unconverged_frac` check (they still run normally). | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `mstep_damping` |  | `1.0` (off); `0.03` with `iiv_on_ruv` | Optional exploration-phase cap on the stochastic-approximation step for the numerical θ/σ M-step (the channel that moves a theta with no ETA). | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `mstep_draws` |  | `1` | Number of E-step draws the **`bobyqa`** M-step objective is averaged over. | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `mstep_solver` |  | `bobyqa` | Which solver moves the numerical θ/σ M-step — the channel that estimates a theta with no ETA. | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `mu_referencing` | `true`, `false` | `true` | Re-centre inner-loop ETA estimates on the current population mean (auto-detected from `[individual_parameters]`). | @sec-variability |
| `multi_start_seed` |  | `42` | RNG seed for the multi-start theta perturbations. Independent of `seed` (SAEM) so that changing the SAEM seed does not silently alter which perturbed starting points are used in FOCE multi-start runs. | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `n_agq` |  | `1` | Gauss-Hermite nodes **per random effect**. `1` reproduces the Laplace approximation exactly; odd values are conventional (they keep a node at the mode). | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `n_convergence` |  | `250` | Phase 2 iterations (step size = 1/k) | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `n_exploration` |  | `150` | Phase 1 iterations (step size = 1) | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `n_leapfrog` |  | `0` | Leapfrog steps per HMC proposal (0 = use MH). When > 0, subjects for which HMC is unavailable (ODE model, missing analytical PK path, non-finite Ω, unsupported TV-cov path) fall back to MH using `n_mh_steps` proposals. | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `n_mh_steps` |  | `auto` | Block Metropolis-Hastings steps per subject per iteration, or `auto` — the default — to size it from the dataset as `2.5 × observations per subject per η`, clamped to `[6, 20]`. | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `n_starts` |  | `1` | Number of independent optimization runs. `1` disables multi-start (no behaviour change). | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `nn_l2` | float ≥ 0 | `0.0` | L2 (weight-decay) strength. Adds `nn_l2 · Σ wᵢ²` over the network's **weight** matrices only (bias terms are left free). | @sec-experimental |
| `nn_smooth` | float ≥ 0 | `0.0` | Smoothness (curvature) strength. Penalizes the finite-difference 2nd derivative `C = f(x+h) − 2·f(x) + f(x−h)` of each output along every input's marginal partial-dependence curve, i.e. `nn_smooth · Σ C²`. | @sec-experimental |
| `npde_nsim` | integer ≥ 0 | `0` | Number of Monte-Carlo replicates per subject used to compute the simulation-based NPDE/NPD diagnostics after the fit. | @sec-diagnostics |
| `npde_seed` | integer | — | RNG seed for the NPDE/NPD simulation, for reproducible diagnostics. | @sec-diagnostics |
| `ode_abstol` | float | `1e-6` | RK45 ODE solver **absolute** tolerance (companion to `ode_reltol`). | @sec-structural-models |
| `ode_auto_switch` | `true`, `false` | `true` | Let `ode_method = auto` change stepper **inside** an integration segment, not only at its start. | @sec-structural-models |
| `ode_max_steps` | integer | `10000` | Max solver steps per integration segment. ODE models and the absorption ODE twin. | @sec-structural-models |
| `ode_method` | `auto`, `linear`, `rk45`, `vern7`, `rosenbrock23`, `rodas4`, `rodas5p` | `auto` | Which stepper integrates the `[odes]` block — or, for a block that is linear in the states, whether to skip integration: `auto` solves such a model **exactly** by the matrix exponential, `linear` asserts that it must (a parse error naming the reason on a model that cannot), and naming any integrator opts out. | @sec-structural-models |
| `ode_reltol` | float | `1e-4` | RK45 ODE solver **relative** tolerance. Applies to ODE models, and to the auto-generated ODE **twin** that closed-form transit / inverse-Gaussian absorption models (`one_cpt_transit`, `two_cpt_transit`, `one_cpt_ig`, `two_cpt_ig`) use to serve IOV, time-varying-covariate, and `TIME`-switch subjects (#719/#814) — so a call-time override reaches those rerouted fits too; otherwise ignored for analytical PK. | @sec-structural-models |
| `ode_stiff_abort_after` | integer ≥ 0, or `off` | `off` | Abandon an integration segment once this many of its steps have **clamped at the minimum step size**, instead of grinding on to `ode_max_steps`. | @sec-structural-models |
| `omega_burnin` |  | `20` | Initial exploration iterations during which Ω (and Ω<sub>IOV</sub>) are held at their starting values while the MH chain warms up. | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `optimizer` | `auto`, `bobyqa`, `slsqp`, `nlopt_lbfgs`, `mma`, `trust_region` (plus deprecated aliases `bfgs`/`lbfgs` → `nlopt_lbfgs`) | `auto` | Outer-loop optimisation algorithm. Applies to `method = foce` / `focei` and to the FOCEI polish phase of `method = gn_hybrid`. | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `optimizer_trace` | `true`, `false` | `false` | Write a per-iteration CSV to `/tmp/ferx_trace_<pid>_<ts>.csv`. | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `outer_ftol` | float | auto | Relative **objective** tolerance: the relative OFV change below which the optimizer stops. | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `outer_xtol` | float | `1e-4` | Relative **step** tolerance: how far the optimizer's step must shrink before it declares success. | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `parameter_scaling` | `auto`, `none`, `abs`, `rescale2` | `auto` | Parameter-scaling strategy for the outer optimizer (supersedes `scale_params` when non-`none`). | @sec-variability |
| `reconverge_gradient_interval` | integer ≥ 0 | `0` | How often to re-solve each subject's inner EBE loop during the population gradient instead of holding the EBEs (η̂) and FOCE Hessian fixed. | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `report_final_gradient` | `true`, `false` | `true` | Compute a finite-difference gradient at the reported estimates when the optimizer supplied none of its own, and report it as `final_gradient` with `final_gradient_source = "finite_difference"`. | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `scale_adaptation` |  | `robbins_monro` | How the MH step scales are adapted. `interval` is the historical rule (×1.1 / ×0.9 every `adapt_interval`); `robbins_monro` steps `log δ` every iteration by `c·k^-0.6·(accept − target)`. | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `scale_deadband` |  | `0.15,0.60` | Acceptance window `lo,hi` in which the `robbins_monro` step is **skipped**, leaving the scale untouched; outside it the ordinary step applies. | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `scale_params` |  | `false` | Legacy boolean alias for `parameter_scaling = abs`. Divide each packed (log/Cholesky) coordinate by its initial magnitude before passing it to the optimizer. | @sec-variability |
| `seed` |  | `12345` | RNG seed for reproducibility | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `sir_df` |  | `5.0` | Degrees of freedom for the Student-t proposal (`>= 1`); higher values approach a normal proposal, and `normal` / `mvn` selects the multivariate-normal proposal itself (ν = ∞) | @sec-uncertainty |
| `sir_keep_samples` |  | `false` | Retain resampled parameter vectors for `simulate_with_uncertainty()` | @sec-uncertainty |
| `sir_resamples` |  | `250` | Number of resampled vectors (m) | @sec-uncertainty |
| `sir_samples` |  | `1000` | Number of proposal samples (M) | @sec-uncertainty |
| `sir_scale` |  | `packed` | Scale the SIR target is flat on: `packed` (log-sd for variances) or `natural`. | @sec-uncertainty |
| `sir_seed` |  | `12345` | RNG seed for reproducibility | @sec-uncertainty |
| `stagnation_guard` |  | `true` | Stop the NLopt-based outer optimizers early once the OFV stops improving; see below. | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `start_sigma` |  | `0.3` | Log-space perturbation applied to initial theta values for starts 1..n. | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `steihaug_max_iters` | integer | adaptive | Max CG iterations for the Steihaug subproblem (only used when `optimizer = trust_region`). | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `vi_avg_last` |  | final 25% | Polyak averaging window, in iterations — the reported estimate is the mean over the final window rather than the last iterate. | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `vi_eta_grad` |  | `auto` | `auto` uses the analytic `Dual2` η-gradient where available and central finite differences where not; `analytic` and `fd` pin one route. | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `vi_family` |  | `full_rank` | `full_rank` fits a full posterior covariance per subject; `mean_field` fits a diagonal one — `O(d)` rather than `O(d²)`. | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `vi_final_ofv` |  | `none` | `none` leaves `ofv` as `NaN`, because the ELBO is a lower bound and is not comparable with a FOCEI OFV; `laplace` computes a comparable one. | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `vi_grad_clip` |  | `1e4` | Global-L2 gradient clip applied to every Adam step; `0` disables it. | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `vi_iters` |  | `25000` | Adam **ceiling**, not a fixed budget — the run stops early once the objective and the estimates have both settled. | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `vi_kl` |  | `analytic` | How the `KL(q ‖ N(0, Ω))` half is evaluated — `analytic` in closed form (only the data term is sampled) or `mc`. | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `vi_lr` |  | `0.02` | Adam learning rate. Lower it if the trace oscillates, or if σ settles above a FOCEI/AGQ fit of the same data. | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `vi_mc_samples` |  | `32` | Monte-Carlo draws per subject per iteration. This sets the noise floor the settling test measures against, so it decides when the run stops as well as how noisy each step is; too few draws can settle early at the wrong answer. | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `vi_omega_update` |  | `closed_form` | `closed_form` sets Ω to its exact ELBO maximizer each iteration, keeping it out of the stochastic optimization; `adam` learns it with everything else. | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `vi_seed` |  | `20240704` | Seed for the common random numbers. See Reproducibility. | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `vi_sigma_update` |  | `closed_form` | As `vi_omega_update`, for the residual error σ. See How σ is updated. | @sec-estimation-methods |

## Model file blocks

The blocks a `.ferx` model file can contain. *Required* and *Purpose* are the ferx-core block overview at the pinned engine, and are blank for a block that overview does not list; the chapter column covers those. Block names are closed-world, so a header outside this table is an error.

| Block | Required | Purpose | Chapter | ferx-core page |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `[adaptive_dosing]` | No | Feedback / TDM dose controller for `simulate()` | @sec-adaptive-dosing | [adaptive-dosing](https://ferx-nlme.org/ferx-core/model-file/adaptive-dosing.html) |
| `[binary_model]` | No | Binary / logistic endpoint (needs `--features survival`) | @sec-binary | [categorical](https://ferx-nlme.org/ferx-core/model-file/categorical.html) |
| `[covariate_model]` |  |  | @sec-covariates | [covariate-model](https://ferx-nlme.org/ferx-core/model-file/covariate-model.html) |
| `[covariate_nn NAME]` | No | Neural-network covariate model (needs `--features nn`) | @sec-experimental | [covariate-nn](https://ferx-nlme.org/ferx-core/model-file/covariate-nn.html) |
| `[covariates]` | No | Declare which data columns are covariates (and how they interpolate) | @sec-covariates | [covariates](https://ferx-nlme.org/ferx-core/model-file/covariates.html) |
| `[data]` | No | Point at the dataset CSV; overridden by an explicit CLI/R path | @sec-data | [data](https://ferx-nlme.org/ferx-core/model-file/data.html) |
| `[data_selection]` | No | Row/subject filters applied to the dataset | @sec-data | [data-selection](https://ferx-nlme.org/ferx-core/model-file/data-selection.html) |
| `[derived]` | No | Post-hoc derived quantities written to sdtab | @sec-tables-figures | [derived](https://ferx-nlme.org/ferx-core/model-file/derived.html) |
| `[diffusion]` | No | SDE diffusion terms | @sec-experimental | [diffusion](https://ferx-nlme.org/ferx-core/model-file/diffusion.html) |
| `[error_model]` | Yes | Define the residual error model | @sec-model-files | [error-model](https://ferx-nlme.org/ferx-core/model-file/error-model.html) |
| `[event_model]` | No | Time-to-event endpoint (needs `--features survival`) | @sec-time-to-event | [event-model](https://ferx-nlme.org/ferx-core/model-file/event-model.html) |
| `[fit_options]` | No | Configure estimation method and optimizer | @sec-model-files | [fit-options](https://ferx-nlme.org/ferx-core/model-file/fit-options.html) |
| `[individual_parameters]` | Yes | Map population parameters to individual PK parameters | @sec-model-files | [individual-parameters](https://ferx-nlme.org/ferx-core/model-file/individual-parameters.html) |
| `[initial_conditions]` | No | Non-zero compartment initial amounts | @sec-structural-models | [initial-conditions](https://ferx-nlme.org/ferx-core/model-file/initial-conditions.html) |
| `[markov_model]` | No | Continuous-time Markov endpoint (needs `--features markov`) | @sec-reference | [markov-model](https://ferx-nlme.org/ferx-core/model-file/markov-model.html) |
| `[mixture]` | No | Mixture (subpopulation) model | @sec-variability | [mixture](https://ferx-nlme.org/ferx-core/estimation/mixture.html) |
| `[odes]` | If ODE | ODE right-hand-side equations | @sec-structural-models | [ode-models](https://ferx-nlme.org/ferx-core/model-file/ode-models.html) |
| `[output]` | No | Extra sdtab output columns | @sec-tables-figures | [output](https://ferx-nlme.org/ferx-core/model-file/output.html) |
| `[parameters]` | Yes | Define theta, omega, and sigma parameters | @sec-model-files | [parameters](https://ferx-nlme.org/ferx-core/model-file/parameters.html) |
| `[priors]` |  |  | @sec-experimental | [priors](https://ferx-nlme.org/ferx-core/estimation/priors.html) |
| `[scaling]` | No | Compartment scaling / observation readouts | @sec-structural-models | [scaling](https://ferx-nlme.org/ferx-core/model-file/scaling.html) |
| `[simulation]` | No | Define a simulation trial design | @sec-simulation | [simulation](https://ferx-nlme.org/ferx-core/model-file/simulation.html) |
| `[structural_model]` | Yes | Specify the PK model (analytical or ODE) | @sec-model-files | [structural-model](https://ferx-nlme.org/ferx-core/model-file/structural-model.html) |

## Data columns

Columns the ferx data format recognises. *Type* and *Meaning* are taken from the ferx-core [data format](https://ferx-nlme.org/ferx-core/data-format.html) page at the pinned engine, and are blank for the columns that page does not list; the chapter column covers those.

| Column | Type | Meaning | Chapter |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ADDL` |  |  | @sec-data |
| `AMT` | numeric | Dose amount (for `EVID=1`/`EVID=4`; also the dose-inference signal when `EVID` is absent) | @sec-data |
| `CENS` | integer | Censoring flag. `1` = below LLOQ and `DV` carries the LLOQ; `-1` = above ULOQ and `DV` carries the ULOQ; `0` = quantified. | @sec-data |
| `CMT` | integer | Compartment number (1-indexed). A float-formatted integer (`2.0`, as pandas writes a whole column once any cell in it is blank) reads as that integer. | @sec-data |
| `DV` | numeric | Dependent variable (observed concentration) | @sec-data |
| `EVID` | integer | Event ID: 0 = observation, 1 = dose, 2 = other event, 3 = system reset, 4 = reset + dose. | @sec-data |
| `FREMTYPE` |  |  | @sec-covariates |
| `ID` | string/numeric | Subject identifier | @sec-data |
| `II` | numeric | Interdose interval for repeated dosing | @sec-data |
| `MDV` | integer | Missing DV flag. 1 = DV should be ignored (row excluded from the likelihood). | @sec-data |
| `RATE` | numeric | Infusion rate. `0` = bolus, `>0` = constant-rate infusion (duration = `AMT/RATE`). | @sec-data |
| `SS` | integer | Steady-state flag. 1 = assume steady state | @sec-data |
| `TENTRY` |  |  | @sec-time-to-event |
| `TIME` | numeric | Observation/event time on the data clock | @sec-data |

| `two_cpt_oral_cov` | @sec-model-selection |
| `two_cpt_oral_global` | @sec-model-selection |
| `warfarin` | @sec-model-selection |
| `warfarin_amd` | @sec-model-selection |
| `warfarin_block_omega` | @sec-model-selection |
| `warfarin_iov` | @sec-model-selection |

## Warning categories

Categories of `ferx_get_warnings(fit, as_df = TRUE)$category`, collected by a fit that ran, with the severity and meaning ferx-core gives them at the pinned engine. **Critical** means the result is untrustworthy as it stands; **Warning** means it stands with a caveat; **Info** implies no action. A model that never ran fails with a check report code instead, listed under *Check report codes* below. Each chapter's *Warnings you may see here* section covers the ones it meets, and the ferx-core [warnings](https://ferx-nlme.org/ferx-core/warnings.html) page describes them all.

| Category | Severity | Meaning | Chapter |
|---|---|---|---|
| `absorption_twin_declined` | Warning | An analytic transit / inverse-Gaussian model's ODE twin could not be built, so the model keeps no ODE fallback (#1008). | @sec-absorption |
| `bloq_method` | Warning | BLOQ / M3 censoring caveat. | @sec-censoring |
| `boundary_estimate` | Warning | One or more THETA **estimates** are pinned to an optimizer bound. | @sec-diagnostics |
| `cancelled` | Info | Run cancelled by the user. | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `condition_number` | Critical | Ill-conditioned covariance / high condition number. The figure is only meaningful next to the estimator that produced it — read `covariance_method` from the `details` payload, or from the fit (Which covariance estimator produced these numbers). | @sec-diagnostics |
| `convergence` | Critical | Optimizer did not converge; **or** (`W_NONFINITE_OBJECTIVE`) the objective at the final estimates is `NaN`, infinite, or at or above the `1e14` divergence cutoff; **or** (`W_NO_FEASIBLE_EVAL`) not one outer trial was feasible — the EBE guard rejected them all, or every objective was non-finite — so nothing was minimised and the estimates are the ones the fit started from (#1617). | @sec-first-fit |
| `covariance_failed` | Critical | Covariance step failed — no standard errors. Every message that starts `Covariance step failed` gets this code, whatever reason it goes on to give (a message carrying a `W_` token is classified by its token first): a profiled fit's "the profile solve did not converge at the estimates" is a covariance failure, not `convergence`, and says nothing about whether the fit converged (#2158). | @sec-uncertainty |
| `covariance_regularized` | Warning | Covariance step succeeded but an eigenvalue floor was applied, or an off-diagonal stencil was non-finite, or (`W_COV_NON_STATIONARY_ESTIMATE`, #1781) `S⁻¹` replaced an `r` / `rsr` whose R needed an eigenvalue floor at a sampler's estimate. | @sec-uncertainty |
| `covariance_step` | Info / Warning | Covariance-step note (e.g. evaluation cost). `W_COV_ODE_TOLERANCE_NOT_TIGHTENED` (Warning): an integrated model's covariance step, which finite-differences its R or S matrix, could not be run at `ode_reltol = 1e-6` / `ode_abstol = 1e-8` and ran at the fit's looser tolerance, so the SEs may be inflated; pin those tolerances to compute them at the plateau (#520). | @sec-uncertainty |
| `data_quality` | Warning | Dataset issue (missing DV, ADDL/II, non-positive DV, …). | @sec-data |
| `degenerate_clearance_or_volume` | Warning | `W_DEGENERATE_CL_V`: the final estimates put a non-positive or non-finite `CL` or `V` on at least one dose, observation, EVID=2 or EVID=3/4 record of a 1-/2-/3-cpt IV / oral closed-form model, each record read under its own covariates and occasion κ (#2104); an EVID=4 row is one record, a separate EVID=3 row beside a dose is two. | @sec-covariates |
| `dw_autocorrelation` | Warning | IWRES autocorrelation (Durbin–Watson out of range). | @sec-diagnostics |
| `ebe_start_dependent` | Warning | (`W_EBE_START_DEPENDENT`) The empirical Bayes estimates at the final parameters depend on where the inner loop starts: re-solving them cold scores materially worse than the EBEs the optimizer minimised against, or returns a non-finite objective (#833). | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `eps_shrinkage` | Warning | Residual (EPS) shrinkage high / negative. | @sec-diagnostics |
| `eta_normality` | Warning | ETA departs from normality. | @sec-diagnostics |
| `eta_shrinkage` | Warning | One or more ETA shrinkages exceed ~30%. | @sec-diagnostics |
| `experimental` | Warning | An experimental feature (SDE, neural-network) was used. | @sec-experimental |
| `flat_parameter` | Warning | A non-fixed THETA has an ≈ 0 outer gradient at the initial estimate — it never reaches the objective (unmapped, or dropped from the structural / scaling model). | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `flip_flop` | Warning | A transit / inverse-Gaussian absorption closed form entered the flip-flop regime (disposition rate ≥ the tilting abscissa). | @sec-absorption |
| `general` | Warning | Unrecognised message (fallback bucket). | @sec-first-fit |
| `gradient_fallback` | Info | A gradient / sampler fallback was taken. | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `high_correlation` | Warning | One or more THETA (fixed-effect) pairs have \|correlation\| ≥ 0.95. | @sec-diagnostics |
| `importance_sampling` | Warning | ESS = 0 / proposal collapse. | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `inflated_rse` | Warning | One or more THETA estimates have RSE > ~50%. | @sec-diagnostics |
| `init_not_representable` |  |  | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `init_outside_bounds` | Warning | An **initial estimate** packs outside one of ferx's internal rails (the hidden `1e9` THETA cap, the OMEGA `±6` / off-diagonal `±10` guards, the SIGMA `[-8, 5]` guard) and was clamped there before the first objective evaluation. | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `mu_referencing` | Warning / Info | Missing or partial mu-referencing. | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `multi_start` | Info | Multi-start note. | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `ode_solver` | Warning / Info | The ODE solver's own health at the final estimates (#1080). **Warning** when steps clamped at the minimum step size (a stability-limited segment whose un-integrated tail is freeze-padded), when a segment stopped before its requested end, when `ode_stiff_abort_after` cut segments short, or when `ode_method = auto` discarded an escalation and re-solved it explicitly — including when only its **analytic derivatives** overflowed, its values staying finite — and when that re-solve failed too. | @sec-structural-models |
| `omega_structure` | Warning | Mixed lognormal / additive block in omega. | @sec-variability |
| `optimizer_config` | Warning / Info | `global_search` config note or failure. | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `optimizer_health` | Warning | Trust-radius collapse / degeneracy, or a fit that stopped mid-descent and was restarted from the best point it reached. | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `parameter_at_runaway_guard` | Critical / Warning | A free coordinate is pinned to a hidden optimizer guard (implicit THETA cap, OMEGA / SIGMA rail), with a `verdict` the side does not decide. | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `simulation` | Warning | A simulated subject was handled specially — a degenerate hazard draw (censored, no event) or an over-large recurrent-event stream (skipped/truncated). | @sec-time-to-event |
| `sir` | Warning | SIR failed or was requested without a covariance; its proposal needed repair; or its effective sample size is below 100, naming the heaviest draw and any variance the data do not bound away from zero. | @sec-uncertainty |
| `stalled_at_init` | Warning | The fit never left its initial estimates — **no** free THETA, OMEGA or SIGMA coordinate moved, so the reported objective is the objective *of the initial values* and carries no information about the model. | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `threads` | Info | Thread-count efficiency note. | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `uncertainty_draws_skipped` | Warning | `simulate_with_uncertainty_diag()` skipped some parameter draws because they fell in the flip-flop regime of a twin-less transit / inverse-Gaussian closed form (#1485). | @sec-simulation |
| `vi_bad_basin` | Critical | VI's final ELBO tightness check found that a flat objective is an unusable variational bound, not convergence. | @sec-estimation-methods |

## Check report codes

Stable identifiers from the model file parser and the pre-fit checks: `E_*` stops the model from running, `W_*` is a check-time note that does not. `ferx_model_validate()` returns them in `$diagnostics`, with the severity, block and line (@sec-model-files). A refused call raises a condition of class `ferx_engine_error` -- from `ferx_fit()`, `ferx_predict()`, `ferx_simulate()` and the other entry points alike -- that carries the same identifier as `$code`, with `$block`, `$line` and `$suggestion` where the engine knows them (`NA` otherwise), and appends the code to the message in square brackets, so a script can branch on it with `tryCatch(..., ferx_engine_error = function(e) e$code)`. These are a different channel from the *Warning categories* above, which a completed fit collects in `fit$warnings`. The 210 codes below (134 errors, 76 warnings) are the check report of the pinned engine, one sentence each; the ferx-core [check report](https://ferx-nlme.org/ferx-core/file-formats/check-report.html) page gives the full text.

| Code | Severity | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `E_ABSORPTION_DIFFUSION` | error | An `[odes]` model whose right-hand side uses a built-in absorption input-rate function (`transit()`, `igd()`, `weibull()`, `zero_order()`, `first_order()`) also declares a `[diffusion]` block. |
| `E_ABSORPTION_DOMAIN` | error | A parameter of a built-in absorption input-rate function in `[odes]` is out of its domain at typical values (η = κ = 0), evaluated at every dose record's own snapshot so a covariate or `TIME`-reading expression is caught at any dose: transit `mtt ≤ 0` or `n < 0`, igd `mat` or `cv2 ≤ 0`, weibull `td` or `beta ≤ 0`, zero_order `dur ≤ 0`, first_order `ka ≤ 0`, or a non-finite per-route `lag=`. |
| `E_ABSORPTION_FRACTION` | error | A dose-splitting pathway fraction (`FR*fn(...)`) on a built-in absorption input-rate term is not in (0, 1], or the fractions on one compartment sum to something other than 1 (tolerance 1e-4), at typical values evaluated at each dose record. |
| `E_ABSORPTION_RATE_ZERO_ORDER` | error | A non-SS infusion (`RATE > 0`) into a compartment fed by a `zero_order()` absorption function in `[odes]`. |
| `E_ABSORPTION_SS_INFUSION` | error | A steady-state infusion (`SS=1` with `RATE > 0`) into a compartment fed by a built-in absorption input-rate function in `[odes]`. |
| `E_ABSORPTION_SS_LAG` | error | An `SS=1` dose with `II > 0` into a compartment fed by a built-in absorption input-rate function, where that compartment has a lag time — a compartment `lagtime` / `ALAG`, or a per-route `lag=` on a forcing feeding it. |
| `E_ABSORPTION_SS_ZERO_ORDER` | error | An `SS=1` dose with `II > 0` into a compartment fed by a `zero_order()` absorption function in `[odes]`. |
| `E_AD_RETIRED` | error | `gradient_method = ad` was requested. The Enzyme automatic-differentiation path was retired; use `auto` (the analytic sensitivities, with finite differences outside their scope) or `fd`. |
| `E_ADAPTIVE_CONTROLLER_ACTION` | error | The controller returned an action the driver refuses (#1983): a dose into compartment 0 or one past the model's states, an amount that is negative or not finite, an infusion rate that is not positive and finite, a dose into a compartment fed by a built-in input-rate function or carrying a lag, or a `Stop` followed by another action. |
| `E_ADAPTIVE_OPTIONS` | error | `AdaptiveSimulateOptions` with no usable schedule (`decision_times` empty, not finite, not strictly increasing, or longer than `max_decisions`), a monitor on a compartment the model does not have, a `Dv` monitor on a compartment no `[error_model]` covers, or `decision_times` / `monitors` set alongside an `[adaptive_dosing]` spec that owns them. |
| `E_ADAPTIVE_SPEC` | error | An `[adaptive_dosing]` spec that does not compile against the model: an invariant the block parser checks (on a spec built in code), an `assay_cmt` out of range or with no `[error_model]` to draw the assay from, a `route` compartment out of range or fed by a built-in input-rate function, or an `observe` expression that does not compile. |
| `E_ADAPTIVE_UNSUPPORTED` | error | A model the adaptive-dosing driver cannot simulate faithfully (no `[odes]` block, an SDE, a covariate-selected `[error_model]`, a residual `correlation` line, a log-transformed (LTBS) error model — #2129), an `auc_target` on a subject with a time-varying covariate, IOV or a reset, or a pre-scheduled base regimen with an EVID=3/4 reset under a time-varying covariate or IOV, refused before any subject is simulated. |
| `E_AGQ_EVAL_ONLY` | error | `agq_eval_only = true` turns a `laplace` stage into a likelihood evaluator, so it needs a `laplace` stage in the chain and that stage must be the last one. |
| `E_AGQ_GRID_TOO_LARGE` | error | A quadrature stage — `method = laplace`, or `method = focei` with `n_agq > 1` — whose tensor grid of `n_agq^n_eta` nodes per subject exceeds `MAX_AGQ_GRID` (100,000). |
| `E_AGQ_NODES_TOO_LARGE` | error | A quadrature stage — `method = laplace`, or `method = focei` with `n_agq > 1` — with `n_agq` above `MAX_AGQ_NODES` (21), where the Golub–Welsch rule loses accuracy. |
| `E_AGQ_NODES_ZERO` | error | `n_agq = 0`, under any method. Zero nodes must not silently disable FOCEI quadrature or be coerced to one-node Laplace, and a method that ignores `n_agq` still records it in the fit, where a `.fitrx` holding 0 does not load (#1770); use `n_agq = 1`. |
| `E_BINARY_GN_UNSUPPORTED` | error | `gn` or `gn_hybrid` anywhere in the method chain on a model with a `[binary_model]` (binary or categorical) endpoint. |
| `E_BINARY_IOV_UNSUPPORTED` | error | A `[binary_model]` (binary or categorical) endpoint on a model with inter-occasion variability (`n_kappa > 0`), whatever the method. |
| `E_BINARY_STATE` | error | A `[binary_model]` record whose DV is not 0 or 1. The reader accepts any non-negative integer on a discrete compartment, since it cannot tell binary from ordinal. |
| `E_BLOCK_FEATURE_DISABLED` | error | A recognised block needs a cargo feature this binary was not built with — `[event_model]` / `[binary_model]` need `--features survival`, `[markov_model]` needs `--features markov`. |
| `E_BLOCK_INSTANCE_NAME` | error | A `[block NAME]` instance name is given for a block that takes none (e.g. `[fit_options DOSE]`), or omitted for one that requires it (`[covariate_nn NAME]`). |
| `E_BLOCK_SIGMA_CHAIN_UNSUPPORTED` | error | A `block_sigma` model with at least one free (non-`FIX`) correlation, whose method chain places a stage that cannot read the estimated correlation (anything but `foce`, `focei`, `laplace`) after a stage that estimates it. |
| `E_BLOCK_SIGMA_FREM_UNSUPPORTED` | error | A `block_sigma` (correlated residual error) model that is also a FREM model with covariate pseudo-observations; the combination is not supported. |
| `E_BLOCK_SIGMA_IIV_ON_RUV_UNSUPPORTED` | error | A `block_sigma` (correlated residual error) model that also scales the residual error by a random effect (`iiv_on_ruv`); the combination is not supported. |
| `E_BLOCK_SIGMA_IOV_UNSUPPORTED` | error | A `block_sigma` (correlated residual error) model with inter-occasion variability (`n_kappa > 0`), whatever the method. |
| `E_BLOCK_SIGMA_METHOD_UNSUPPORTED` | error | A `block_sigma` (correlated residual error) model whose method chain contains a stage outside `foce`, `focei`, `saem`, `imp`, `laplace` and `vi` — that is, `gn`, `gn_hybrid`, `impmap` or `bayes`. |
| `E_BLOCK_SIGMA_SDE_UNSUPPORTED` | error | A `block_sigma` (correlated residual error) model with a `[diffusion]` block and a `saem` stage in the method chain. |
| `E_BLOCK_SIGMA_TTE_UNSUPPORTED` | error | A `block_sigma` (correlated residual error) model that also declares a non-Gaussian endpoint (`[event_model]`, `[binary_model]` or `[markov_model]`), whatever the method. |
| `E_BLOCK_VARIANCE_ONLY` | error | A scale tag (`(sd)`, `(variance)` or `(var)`) on a `block_omega`, `block_sigma` or `block_kappa` declaration. |
| `E_COV_LEVEL_UNKNOWN` | error | The data carry a value of a categorical `[covariate_model]` covariate that is not one of the relation's levels, which the generated factor would silently model as the reference level (#1111, #1740). |
| `E_COVARIATE_NOT_NUMERIC` | error | A column the `[covariates]` block declares holds a value that is not a number. Block `covariates`. |
| `E_COVARIATE_STATS_BINDING` | error | A `[covariate_model]` statistic could not be bound to the data: a `levels = auto` relation whose data carry one level, or a covariate with no non-missing value. |
| `E_COVSTAT_UNRESOLVED` | error | A `[covariate_model]` relation still needs statistics derived from the data — `center = median`, `levels = auto`, or a form whose default bounds come from the data — and none were bound. |
| `E_CTMM_GN_UNSUPPORTED` | error | `gn` or `gn_hybrid` anywhere in the method chain on a model with a `[markov_model]` (CTMM) endpoint. |
| `E_CTMM_IOV_UNSUPPORTED` | error | A `[markov_model]` (CTMM) endpoint on a model with inter-occasion variability (`n_kappa > 0`), whatever the method. |
| `E_CTMM_RECORDS` | error | A `[markov_model]` (CTMM) record whose DV is not one of the declared `states`, or a subject whose CTMM observation times decrease (the reader sorts doses, not observations). |
| `E_CTMM_UNSUPPORTED` | error | A `[markov_model]` endpoint reached `predict()` with no continuous observation to predict, or `simulate()` or `run_model_simulate()`: neither has a state-occupancy path yet (#820). |
| `E_DATA` | error | The `--data` file could not be read or parsed. |
| `E_DATA_PATH_MISSING` | error | No data path was given and the model file has no `[data]` block. `ferx check` without `--data` skips its data checks instead of refusing. |
| `E_DEPRECATED_BLOCK` | error | A `[block]` that *was* ferx syntax and is no longer read — currently `[initial_values]`, whose contents moved inline into `[parameters]`. |
| `E_DERIVED_NAME_CONFLICT` | error | A `[derived]` name clashes with a built-in sdtab column, theta, eta, or individual-parameter name. |
| `E_DOSE_ATTR_DOUBLE_USE` | error | A dose attribute the engine applies at the dose event is *also* read by the model, so its value is applied twice. |
| `E_DOSE_ATTR_NONFINITE` | error | A dose attribute the engine applies at the dose event — lag time (`lagtime` / `ALAG{n}`), bioavailability (`F` / `F{n}`), or a modeled infusion duration `D{n}` / rate `R{n}` behind a coded `RATE` — is `NaN` or infinite at typical values for some subject. |
| `E_DOSE_CMT_NOT_INFUSABLE` | error | Raised on `[odes]` models and the event-walk analytical models (not transit / inverse-Gaussian); reported once per compartment, with the subject and time of the first row. |
| `E_DOSE_CMT_OUT_OF_RANGE` | error | A dose record — bolus or infusion, zero amount included — whose `CMT` exceeds the number of compartments: the `[odes]` block's declared states, or the analytical model's compartments. |
| `E_DOSE_NO_AMT` | error | The dataset has dose records (`EVID` 1 or 4) but no `AMT` column, so every dose would have amount zero and the fit would run with no drug in the system. |
| `E_ENDPOINT_NO_RECORDS` | error | A declared non-Gaussian endpoint has no row routed to it anywhere in the data — typically the `CMT` column is missing, so every row reads as CMT 1. |
| `E_ENDPOINT_TIME_DEPENDENT_PK` | error | The `TIME` axis of the same freeze: an ODE-accumulated (drug-driven) hazard integrates the individual parameters at their TIME=0 values, so a `[individual_parameters]` value that reads `TIME` and reaches the hazard (through the `[odes]` right-hand side or an `init()` seed) would put the PK and hazard halves of the objective on different concentration curves (#1853). |
| `E_ENDPOINT_TV_COVARIATE` | error | A covariate that varies within a subject — on any row, endpoint rows included (#1854) — is read by an endpoint that evaluates it once, at the subject's baseline: an analytic hazard's own parameters, any covariate under an ODE-accumulated (drug-driven) hazard, a `[binary_model]` linear predictor, a `[markov_model]` transition intensity, or — on a drug-driven (time-inhomogeneous) CTMM — an individual parameter the `[odes]` solve feeds into the states the intensities read (#1854). |
| `E_ENDPOINT_UNROUTED` | error | A compartment the model declares as a non-Gaussian endpoint (`[event_model]`, `[binary_model]`, Markov) carries Gaussian observations: the population was read without endpoint routing, so the endpoint's rows would be scored as concentrations and its likelihood would contribute nothing. |
| `E_ETA_NOT_DECLARED` | error | An unresolved identifier reads as a random effect (`ETA…` / `KAPPA…`) but no `omega` / `kappa` declaration defines it, and the data carries no such column. |
| `E_FIT_INPUT_CHANGED` | error | The model or data file the step re-reads no longer has the SHA-256 the fit recorded. |
| `E_FIT_INPUT_MISSING` | error | An input the step needs was neither passed nor recorded on the fit: the model file's path (no model passed), the data file's path (no population passed), SIR's covariance matrix, the population of an IOV model passed as a model on a fit that records no reader settings, the occasion rule of an IOV fit saved before ferx recorded one, on a population that carries no occasion labels, or the fitted values of a `[mixture]` fit's per-class overrides, on a fit that records neither them (`mixture_overrides`) nor a packed estimate holding them. |
| `E_FIT_INPUT_MODEL` | error | The model the step would run on is not the one the fit was made with: a model passed in bound with other data-derived bindings than the fit's, a model passed in whose covariate statistics the population does not reproduce (on a fit that records no bindings), a model whose η count is not the width of the fit's per-subject η̂, a `[mixture]` fit whose recorded override values are malformed, or which records none and whose packed estimate has another layout or no longer reproduces its reported estimates, or a covariance matrix that is not the size of the model's packed parameters. |
| `E_FIT_OPTION` | error | A call-time fit-option override handed to `validate_model_file_with()` could not be applied: the key is not a `[fit_options]` / `[data_selection]` key, or its value is one the key does not accept. |
| `E_FIT_SUBJECTS_MISMATCH` | error | The population matches the fit's fingerprint, but the fit's per-subject results (`fit.subjects`), which `run_sir` / `run_covariance` read by position, are another count or another order (#1868). |
| `E_FOCEI_NAGQ_UNSUPPORTED` | error | `method = focei` with `n_agq > 1` (the Gauss-Newton-anchored quadrature) on a model outside the analytic sensitivity scope, e.g. an ODE model without sensitivities or a pure TTE endpoint. |
| `E_FREM_NON_GAUSSIAN_ENDPOINT` | error | `prepare_frem()` or `transform_dataset_for_frem()` was handed a model that declares a non-Gaussian endpoint (`[event_model]`, `[binary_model]` or `[markov_model]`). |
| `E_IG_FLIP_FLOP` | error | An inverse-Gaussian absorption model (`one_cpt_ig` / `two_cpt_ig`) with no ODE twin to reroute to whose typical-value (η = 0) parameters fall outside the closed form's convergence domain on some subject — the flip-flop regime (disposition rate ≥ `1/(2·MAT·CV²)`) or, for 2-cpt, coincident disposition eigenvalues — where it returns an identically-zero profile. |
| `E_IG_UNSUPPORTED` | error | An inverse-Gaussian absorption model (`one_cpt_ig` / `two_cpt_ig`) with a dose or model feature its closed form cannot serve. |
| `E_IIV_ON_RUV_METHOD` | error | `iiv_on_ruv` with a non-interaction stage (`foce`, or `gn` without `interaction`) anywhere in the method chain. |
| `E_IIV_ON_RUV_SHARED_ETA` | error | The `iiv_on_ruv` random effect is also used in `[individual_parameters]`. It must be a dedicated `omega`. |
| `E_IMP_CHAIN` | error | `imp` is mis-placed in a method chain — repeated, or (with `imp_eval_only = true`) not the terminal stage. |
| `E_IMPMAP_IOV_UNSUPPORTED` | error | `method = impmap` (anywhere in a method chain) on a model with inter-occasion variability (`n_kappa > 0`). |
| `E_INIT_BOUNDS_INVERTED` | error | A coordinate whose packed box is **empty**, so no start can be placed in it at all. |
| `E_IOV_MISSING_OCC` | error | Model declares kappa (IOV) parameters but no occasion labels were found. Set `iov_column` to read them from a dataset column, or `iov_occasion = dose` / `time(...)` to derive them in the model, both in `[fit_options]`. |
| `E_IOV_SINGLE_OCCASION` | error | A derived `iov_occasion` rule (`dose` or `time(...)`) gives every subject at most one occasion, so the per-occasion κ cannot be told from the η. |
| `E_KAPPA_WEIGHT_NONPOSITIVE` | error | A `kappa NAME ~ value weight = W` sample-size weight evaluates to zero, a negative number or a non-finite value at some observation or dose record, at the model's initial θ. κ is applied as `κ/√W`, so such a weight divides an individual parameter by zero. |
| `E_LEVEL_MISSING_LABEL` | error | A record (observation, dose, `EVID=2` / `MDV=1` row or reset) has no numeric value in a level column (a blank cell is missing, not carried forward from the row before; a text label such as `NCT01` has to be written as a numeric code). |
| `E_LEVEL_MIXED_WITH_IOV_COLUMN` | error | A `level` declaration together with `iov_column` or `iov_occasion` in `[fit_options]`, an `iov_occasion` rule other than `column` in the fit options or `SimulateOptions` of a model with nested levels (block `fit_options`), or a `kappa` with no `at LEVEL` in a model that declares levels. |
| `E_LEVEL_SINGLE_MEMBER` | error | A level has at most one group inside every group of its parent, and one of its kappas enters the model through the same parameters as a random effect of the parent level (the subject's η for the first level). |
| `E_LOGIT_THETA_OUT_OF_RANGE` | error | A free θ used as `inv_logit(logit(θ) + ETA)` whose estimate is not strictly inside (0, 1), so it has no logit-scale draw (#2044). |
| `E_LTBS_UNSUPPORTED` | error | LTBS (`log_transform = true`) with a proportional or combined error, a per-CMT error model, or an SDE. |
| `E_METHOD_NO_RANDOM_EFFECTS` | error | `method = imp`, `impmap` or `bayes` (anywhere in a method chain) on a model with no random effects (`n_eta = 0`). |
| `E_MISSING_BLOCK` | error | A required `[block]` is absent. `block` names which one. |
| `E_MISSING_COVARIATE` | error | The model references a covariate not present in the data (case-sensitive). On block `covariates`, a column the `[covariates]` block declares is missing from the file. |
| `E_MIXTURE_METHOD` | error | A `[mixture]` model with a method its objective is not wired for: `method = focei` with `n_agq > 1`, an estimator other than `foce` / `focei` / `saem` / `bayes` / `imp` / `impmap`, or `bayes` with per-class `omega(k)` / `sigma(k)` overrides, since its Ω draw is shared across classes. |
| `E_MODEL_READ` | error | The model file could not be read: it does not exist, cannot be opened, or is not UTF-8. |
| `E_MODELED_DURATION_NO_PARAM` | error | A dose codes `RATE=-2` (modeled infusion duration) into compartment `n`, but the model declares no `D{n}` in `[individual_parameters]`, so the duration has no value to read. |
| `E_MODELED_RATE_NO_PARAM` | error | A dose codes `RATE=-1` (modeled infusion rate) into compartment `n`, but the model declares no `R{n}` in `[individual_parameters]`, so the rate has no value to read. |
| `E_NEGATIVE_LAGTIME` | error | A dose lag — `lagtime` / `ALAG{n}`, or a per-route `fn(..., lag=L)` on the compartment the dose lands in — is negative at the initial typical-value point (η = 0), at some dose record's own snapshot. |
| `E_NESTED_LEVEL_METHOD_UNSUPPORTED` | error | A model with nested levels (more than one `level`) fitted with a method other than `foce` / `focei` at `n_agq = 1`: SAEM, IMP, IMPMAP, Bayes, VI, Laplace, FOCEI quadrature or GN anywhere in the chain, or with a `[mixture]` or FREM. |
| `E_NESTED_LEVEL_SIMULATE_UNSUPPORTED` | error | A model with nested levels (more than one `level`) reached an adaptive-dosing entry point. |
| `E_NN_FEATURE_DISABLED` | error | A `[covariate_nn]` block requires building with `--features nn`. |
| `E_NO_SCORED_OBSERVATIONS` | error | The population has no record the likelihood scores: no Gaussian observation and no endpoint (TTE / binary / categorical / Markov) record on any subject. |
| `E_NONFINITE_DV` | error | A subject carries a non-finite (`NaN`/`Inf`) observation. Usually a population read by `read_population_for_simulation()` — a simulation input — passed to `fit()`. |
| `E_ODE_METHOD_LINEAR` | error | `ode_method = linear` was passed in a caller's fit options (`fit()`, `run_covariance`, `run_sir`) for a model that cannot take the exact linear path: it has no `[odes]` block, or an equation is nonlinear in the states, reads model time, or uses an absorption input function, or it is a `[diffusion]` model. |
| `E_ODE_SOLVER_OPTIONS` | error | ODE solver settings on a `FitOptions` built in code that no solver can run with: an `ode_reltol` or `ode_abstol` that is not finite and positive, `ode_max_steps = 0` (#2044), or `ode_stiff_abort_after = Some(0)`, which `[fit_options]` spells as off (#1770). |
| `E_OMEGA_INIT_AT_RAIL` | error | A **free** `omega` / `kappa` / `[mixture] omega(k)` variance whose initial value packs onto the optimizer's `-6` lower rail — every variance ≤ 6.1e-6, and `~ 0.0` in particular (a declared zero is regularised to 1e-8, packing to `ln(L) = -9.21`). |
| `E_OPTIMIZER_AGQ` | error | `optimizer = trust_region` used with a quadrature stage (`method = laplace`, or `method = focei` with `n_agq > 1`). |
| `E_OPTIMIZER_IOV` | error | `optimizer = trust_region` used with an IOV model (`n_kappa > 0`). |
| `E_OUTPUT_UNKNOWN_COLUMN` | error | A name in `[output]` is not recognised as a covariate, individual parameter, or derived expression. |
| `E_PARAM_SHAPE` | error | An entry point was handed an Ω, σ or Ω~IOV~ whose dimension is not the model's, an Ω~IOV~ on a model with no κ, or none on a model with κ, and refused it rather than read it by position (#1764, #1774). |
| `E_PARSE` | error | The model file failed to parse (catch-all for parser errors). |
| `E_PER_CMT_ERROR_MODEL` | error | An observed compartment lacks a per-CMT `[error_model]` entry. |
| `E_PER_CMT_SCALING` | error | An observed compartment lacks a per-CMT scaling entry. |
| `E_POPULATION_MISMATCH` | error | A population handed to, or re-read by, a post-hoc step is not the one the fit was given (#1685): another subject list, other covariate columns, or a subject whose records, doses or covariate values differ. |
| `E_PRIOR_COV_METHOD_UNSUPPORTED` | error | A `prior(...)` is in force and the covariance step runs with `covariance_method = s` or `rsr`. |
| `E_PRIOR_METHOD_UNSUPPORTED` | error | A `prior(...)` is in force but the last stage that estimates (a trailing evaluation-only `imp` or `laplace` does not count) is not one that applies parameter priors — only `foce`, `focei`, `laplace`, `gn` and `gn_hybrid` do. |
| `E_PRIOR_UNRESOLVED` | error | A declared prior cannot be applied: it names no `theta` / `omega` / `sigma` / `kappa` in `[parameters]`, names a `FIX`ed parameter, an element of a `block_omega` / `block_sigma` / `block_kappa`, or a name that resolves to several coordinates; it is declared twice; its central value is not finite (or not positive for a log-packed parameter); or a `[priors] from_fit` was not expanded. |
| `E_PROFILE_NOT_LINEAR` | error | A profiled block that a prediction does not read as `c × block` plus terms that do not read it, with `c` from the data alone. |
| `E_PROFILE_SCOPE` | error | A profiled block that cannot be fitted that way: `profile` on a single θ, or with `FIX`; a box that is a point, is empty or misses the init; a method other than `foce` / `focei`, or `n_agq > 1`; a non-Gaussian endpoint; a residual error that is not additive, or log-transformed; M3 censoring; a `[mixture]`, `[diffusion]` or FREM model; `optimizer = trust_region` or `mma`; `global_search`; a parameter prior. |
| `E_PROPENSITY_INPUT` | error | Propensity-score matching was requested on a population it cannot compute posthoc etas from: empty, a subject with no observations, a subject with a non-finite `DV`, or a `[mixture]` model. |
| `E_READOUT_DEPOT_UNSUPPORTED` | error | An analytic `[scaling] y = …` readout reads the oral `depot` amount on a subject whose depot dose superposition cannot reconstruct: one with an EVID=3/4 reset (#650), or one dosing a compartment other than the default (#375). |
| `E_RESIDUAL_CORRELATION_CONFOUNDED_KAPPA` | error | A `correlation cs(…) by …` line whose blocks group the observation rows exactly as the groups of a level that carries a kappa (a nested level, or the occasions of a one-level model), compared as partitions in every subject, so `cs by ARMID` beside `kappa … at ARM` counts. |
| `E_RESIDUAL_CORRELATION_GROUPING_AMBIGUOUS` | error | A residual `correlation … by` line on a model with nested levels whose grouping a level and a data column would read two ways: a level name inside a list of columns (`by (STUDY, ARM)`), a level name that is also a different data column, or the `by` column of a level nested in another level written under another name. |
| `E_RESIDUAL_CORRELATION_RANGE` | error | The θ behind a residual `correlation <kind>(RHO) by …` line can leave the residual covariance `R` indefinite: a `cs` ρ at or below `−1/(n−1)` for the largest block of `n` rows, a negative `car1` ρ, or a fixed / simulated value with `abs(ρ) ≥ 1`. |
| `E_RESIDUAL_CORRELATION_RESET` | error | Under a residual `correlation ar1(…)` or `car1(…)` line, one block holds rows on both sides of a TIME reset (an `EVID=3/4` record that restarts TIME), so their order and the lag between them are undefined. |
| `E_RESIDUAL_CORRELATION_SCOPE` | error | A residual `correlation` line is fitted by `foce` and `focei` only. Refused with any other method anywhere in the chain, with `n_agq > 1`, with `bloq_method = m3`, with FREM covariate pseudo-observations, with a time-to-event / binary / categorical / Markov endpoint, with a mixture model, or with an SDE (`[diffusion]`) model. |
| `E_RESIDUAL_CORRELATION_TIES` | error | Under a residual `correlation ar1(…)` or `car1(…)` line, two rows of one block share a TIME. |
| `E_RTTE_RECORDS` | error | A repeated-event (`type = rtte`) endpoint's records: interval-censored, a non-finite `TIME`, an entry time after the record's `TIME`, or out of time order; under `clock = reset` also a right-censored row before a later record, or two events at one `TIME`. |
| `E_RUV_MAGNITUDE_NONPOSITIVE` | error | A custom residual-error magnitude in `[error_model]` — an expression multiplying a sigma, such as a `weight = ...` modifier — or a `power(SIGMA, P)` exponent evaluates to zero, a negative number or a non-finite value at some observation, at the model's initial θ. |
| `E_SAEM_NO_RANDOM_EFFECTS` | error | `method = saem` (anywhere in a method chain) on a model with no random effects (`n_eta = 0`). |
| `E_SDE_INCOMPATIBLE` | error | An SDE (`[diffusion]`) model used with an incompatible method (`saem`, `gn`, `gn_hybrid`) or gradient setting. |
| `E_SIGMA_ORDER_MISMATCH` | error | A single-endpoint `[error_model]` names its sigmas in an order other than the `[parameters]` declaration order. |
| `E_SIMULATE_HORIZON` | error | The simulation horizon is missing where a repeated-event or drug-driven TTE endpoint needs one (on an entry point that takes a horizon), is not finite and positive, or lies below a subject's entry time. |
| `E_SIMULATION_DESIGN` | error | A `[simulation]` design that gives the model nothing to observe: no `times` for a continuous (residual-error) or `[binary_model]` endpoint, or no `times` and no TTE endpoint to observe at a `horizon`. |
| `E_SIR_NOTHING_TO_SAMPLE` | error | every estimated parameter of the fit is FIX (θ, Ω and σ, and Ω_IOV, `block_sigma` correlations and `[mixture]` overrides where the model has them), so `run_sir()` has nothing to sample. |
| `E_SIR_OPTIONS` | error | SIR settings `run_sir()` cannot run with: `sir_resamples` above `sir_samples`, a `sir_df` that is not a valid Student-t degrees of freedom, or `sir_scale = natural` on a model with `prior(...)`. |
| `E_SUPPLIED_ETAS` | error | Per-subject η supplied to an adaptive run that cannot be used as given (#1594). From `SuppliedEtas::from_table` or `from_fit`: IDs and rows that differ in count, a row that is not one finite value per named η, a repeated subject ID, or a fit whose η names are not the model's. |
| `E_THETA_GATHER_INDEX_MISSING` | error | A `theta NAME[...]` block gathered by a bare data column, where some observation or dose record of a subject has no value in that column. |
| `E_THETA_GATHER_INDEX_RANGE` | error | A `theta NAME[...]` block's index column holds a value on some record that is not finite, not a whole number, or outside `1..=N` for the block's `N` levels. |
| `E_THETA_INIT_OUTSIDE_BOUNDS` | error | A `theta` whose initial value is **strictly outside** its own declared range. The optimizer clamps the start into its box, so `theta TVCL(0.05, 0.1, 10.0)` fits from `0.1` — a factor of two — silently, on every run. |
| `E_THETA_LENGTH` | error | An entry point taking a parameter vector was handed a θ whose length is not the model's, and refused it rather than read it by position. |
| `E_THETA_LEVEL_BINDING` | error | A `theta NAME[COL, ...]` level block could not be bound to the data's levels: a level column missing or non-finite, no observation rows, or a contrast the data cannot carry. |
| `E_THETA_LEVELS_DATA_MISMATCH` | error | A population that carries a bound level block's index was bound for other levels than the model's (#1762): a record's index is not the position, in the model's level table, of the label its own level columns spell, or an index arrives without its level column. |
| `E_THETA_LEVELS_DATA_UNBOUND` | error | A model whose `theta NAME[...]` level block is bound was handed a population never bound for it, so no record carries an index into the block's levels — the usual "fit, then predict or simulate new data" without binding the new data. |
| `E_THETA_LEVELS_UNBOUND` | error | A `theta NAME[...]` level block was never bound to data, so it has no levels and every value gathered from it is `NaN` — a `CompiledModel` assembled in code that skipped the binder. |
| `E_TRANSIT_FLIP_FLOP` | error | A transit absorption model (`one_cpt_transit` / `two_cpt_transit`) with no ODE twin to reroute to whose typical-value (η = 0) parameters fall outside the closed form's convergence domain on some subject — the flip-flop regime (disposition rate ≥ `KTR = (n+1)/mtt`) or, for 2-cpt, coincident disposition eigenvalues — where it returns an identically-zero profile. |
| `E_TRANSIT_UNSUPPORTED` | error | A transit absorption model (`one_cpt_transit` / `two_cpt_transit`) with a dose or model feature its closed form cannot serve. |
| `E_TTE_NOT_SIMULATABLE` | error | A TTE endpoint the event-time simulator cannot draw for this population: more than one repeated-event stream on a subject, a repeated-event cause beside a single-event one, an EVID=3/4 reset under a repeated-event or a drug-driven hazard, or left truncation under a drug-driven hazard. |
| `E_UNKNOWN_BLOCK` | error | A `[block]` header is not a recognised block name. The message lists every offending header with its line, the valid set **this build accepts**, and a did-you-mean when there is a near match; `suggestion` carries the near match on its own. |
| `E_VI_MODEL_UNSUPPORTED` | error | `method = vi` (anywhere in a method chain) on a model whose likelihood VI's data term — the fixed-η Gaussian observation NLL — does not cover: one with a non-Gaussian endpoint (time-to-event, binary, categorical; under the `survival` feature), or an SDE (`[diffusion]`) model scored by the EKF. |
| `E_VI_NAGQ_UNSUPPORTED` | error | `n_agq > 1` set on a method chain that contains `vi` and no stage that uses a quadrature grid (`laplace` or `focei`). |
| `W_ABSORPTION_TWIN_DECLINED` | warning | An analytic transit / inverse-Gaussian model's ODE twin could not be built, so the model stays closed-form with no ODE fallback. |
| `W_ADDITIVE_INIT_SCALE` | warning | A `combined` error model's additive SD initial estimate is below 1% of the data scale (the median `abs(DV)` of the observations that endpoint covers). |
| `W_ADDL_MISSING_II` | warning | ADDL > 0 on a dose row but II is zero or missing; additional doses were not expanded. |
| `W_ALL_DOSES_ZERO` | warning | An `AMT` column is present and at least one dose event was parsed, but every parsed amount is exactly zero. |
| `W_AMT_NOT_DOSED` | warning | Record(s) carry `AMT != 0` but were **not** read as dose events, because `EVID` is neither 1 nor 4; their `AMT` was ignored. |
| `W_AUTO_OPTIMIZER_FOLLOWS_GRADIENT` | warning | `gradient = fd` set while `optimizer` is left at `auto`, on a model whose analytic outer gradient *is* in scope. |
| `W_CENS_UNEXPECTED` | warning | An observation row's `CENS` cell is a whole number other than `-1` (above ULOQ), `0` (quantified) or `1` (below LLOQ), such as `7` or `-2`. |
| `W_CMT_DEFAULTED` | warning | Dose and observation rows were assigned compartment 1 because the dataset did not say which one — no `CMT` column, or a cell that is missing (`.`/blank/`NA`) or not a compartment index. |
| `W_COMPARTMENT_FREE_DOSES` | warning | The dataset carries dose records but the `[structural_model]` is compartment-free, so no dose is applied and `AMT` / `RATE` / `SS` / `CMT` on those rows have no effect on the prediction. |
| `W_COV_ANALYTIC_SALVAGE` | warning | The covariance step assembled the exact analytic R matrix for the subjects inside the analytic scope and finite-differenced the information terms of the subjects outside it, rather than moving the whole population onto the finite-difference stencil (#1514). |
| `W_COV_NN_PENALTY` | warning | A regularized `[covariate_nn]` fit (`nn_l2` / `nn_smooth`): under `covariance_method = r` / `rsr` the standard errors include the penalty's curvature (penalized-ML SEs, Info); under `s` they cannot represent it (Warning) (#1352). |
| `W_COV_NON_STATIONARY_ESTIMATE` | warning | The covariance R matrix needed an eigenvalue floor (indefinite, or an eigenvalue under `max(1e-10·λ_max, 1e-12)`) at a `saem` / `imp` / `impmap` / `vi` estimate, which those methods never minimise the R objective at. |
| `W_COV_ODE_TOLERANCE_NOT_TIGHTENED` | warning | An integrated model's covariance step, which finite-differences its R stencil or score matrix S, could not be run at `ode_reltol = 1e-6` / `ode_abstol = 1e-8` and ran at the fit's looser tolerance, so the standard errors may be inflated by integration noise (#520). |
| `W_COV_PROFILED_LEVELS_RESOLVED` | warning | `run_covariance` on a profiled fit whose level estimates are not the profile solve's at the other estimates, because they were edited after the fit. |
| `W_COV_QUADRATURE_DECLINED` | warning | The same kind of fit, where the quadrature marginal could not be used — a mixture, inter-occasion variability, or more than three random effects — so the standard errors are the FOCEI objective's curvature at a point that objective need not minimise (#1781). |
| `W_COV_QUADRATURE_OBJECTIVE` | warning | A `saem` / `imp` / `impmap` estimate on a model with a non-Gaussian endpoint had its covariance R and S matrices taken on the 7-node adaptive Gauss–Hermite marginal (`method = laplace, n_agq = 7`) rather than on the FOCEI objective, whose minimum can sit far from that estimate (#1781). |
| `W_COV_RSR_ONE_SUBJECT_LEVELS` | warning | A successful `covariance_method = rsr` step on a model with a θ level block, profiled or not, where some estimated levels are read by a single subject (an MBMA block over `[STUDY, TIME]` with one subject per study). |
| `W_COVARIATE_MISSING` | warning | A covariate column that exists has no value (every cell `.`, blank or `NA`) for some subjects, so it is `NaN` for them. |
| `W_COVSTAT_UNBOUND` | warning | As `E_COVSTAT_UNRESOLVED`, but reported without a `--data` file: the model is fine, it just cannot be built until a dataset supplies the statistics. |
| `W_DATA` | warning | A warning from the data reader whose message does not begin with its own `W_` code. |
| `W_DATA_PATH_OVERRIDE` | warning | A data path was passed explicitly (`--data`, or from R) and the model file's `[data]` block names a different file — compared as written, then as canonicalized paths. |
| `W_DEGENERATE_CL_V` | warning | The final estimates put a non-positive or non-finite `CL` or `V` on at least one dose, observation, EVID=2 or EVID=3/4 record of a 1-/2-/3-cpt IV / oral closed-form model, each record read under its own covariates and occasion. |
| `W_DERIVED_CMT_IOV_UNSUPPORTED` | warning | A `[derived]` expression reads `compartments[i]`, and at least one subject of the fit carries IOV (kappa) parameters. |
| `W_DERIVED_CMT_ORAL_DEPOT_INFUSION_ANALYTICAL` | warning | A `[derived]` expression reads `compartments[i]` on an analytical (non-`[odes]`) model where some subject has a dose the closed-form superposition cannot place: an infusion into a compartment other than central (including a zero-order input into the oral depot) or a bolus into a compartment other than 1. |
| `W_DERIVED_CMT_RESET_ANALYTICAL` | warning | A `[derived]` expression reads `compartments[i]` on an analytical (non-`[odes]`) model where some subject has an `EVID=3/4` reset. |
| `W_DERIVED_CMT_TV_ANALYTICAL` | warning | The model has no `[odes]` block, a `[derived]` expression references `compartments[i]`, and at least one subject carries time-varying covariates, or an individual parameter reads `TIME` (#1855). |
| `W_DERIVED_CMT_TV_ODE` | warning | The model has an `[odes]` block, a `[derived]` expression references `compartments[i]`, and at least one subject carries time-varying covariates, or an individual parameter reads `TIME` (#1855). |
| `W_DERIVED_COVARIATE_SHADOW` | warning | A `[derived]` name shadows a covariate (allowed but may be confusing). |
| `W_DERIVED_INIT_ANALYTICAL` | warning | The model has no `[odes]` block, declares an `[initial_conditions]` baseline, and a `[derived]` expression references `compartments[i]`. |
| `W_DERIVED_STEP_IGNORED` | warning | `step=` given for a DV-based integral (ignored; DV integrals always use observation times). |
| `W_DESIGN_DV` | warning | Simulation reader only: one or more `EVID=0` rows had a missing `DV` and were kept as design points to simulate at, so the dataset contributes more rows than a fit of the same file would. |
| `W_EBE_START_DEPENDENT` | warning | Three triggers. A cold re-solve of the EBEs at the final estimates scores worse than the reported objective by more than `1e-3·(1 + abs(OFV))`, or returns a non-finite objective (#833). |
| `W_ETA_NOT_DECLARED` | warning | As `E_ETA_NOT_DECLARED`, but reported without `--data`, where ferx cannot yet know whether the dataset supplies the column. |
| `W_EXPERIMENTAL_NN` | warning | The model uses neural-network components (`[covariate_nn]`), an experimental feature. |
| `W_EXPERIMENTAL_SDE` | warning | The model uses stochastic differential equations (`[diffusion]`), an experimental feature. |
| `W_FILTER_COLUMN_ABSENT` | warning | A `[data_selection]` condition names a column the dataset does not have. The comparison never matches, so the condition does not select what was meant — and what that costs depends on the key it was written under: an `ignore` excludes nothing, an `accept` excludes **every** row. |
| `W_FREM_DRAWN_ETA` | warning | A FREM model was simulated with each subject's η drawn from Ω, covariate η included: by `simulate_with_options_diag()` without `match_method`, by `simulate_with_uncertainty_diag()`, or by an adaptive simulation for the subjects with no supplied η. |
| `W_GN_NO_RANDOM_EFFECTS` | warning | `method = gn` as the last estimating stage on a model with no random effects (`n_eta = 0`). |
| `W_IG_FLIP_FLOP` | warning | An inverse-Gaussian absorption closed form (`one_cpt_ig` / `two_cpt_ig`) with an ODE twin has, at the initial typical values (η = 0) of at least one subject, a disposition rate (`CL/V`, or the 2-cpt fast rate α) at or above the IG abscissa `1/(2·MAT·CV²)`. ferx evaluates the equivalent `igd` ODE model for such parameters, which is correct but slower. |
| `W_INIT_NOT_REPRESENTABLE` | warning | A declared value the **packer itself** altered, before any box existed (#1307): the `1e-10` log floor on a θ / Ω-diagonal / Σ / `[mixture]` override, or the Fisher-z `±3` rail on a **free** `block_sigma` correlation. |
| `W_INIT_OUTSIDE_BOUNDS` | warning | An initial estimate strictly outside one of ferx's **internal** rails rather than a declared bound: the hidden `1e9` θ cap, the Ω `±6` (variance ≤ 1.6e5) / off-diagonal `±10` guards, or the Σ `[-8, 5]` guard. |
| `W_IOV_NO_OCCASIONS` | warning | The model declares kappa (IOV) parameters and an Ω_IOV is supplied, but some subjects carry no occasion label once `iov_occasion` has been applied. |
| `W_IOV_OCC_MISSING` | warning | Some rows in the IOV occasion column had missing or unparseable values; those rows were assigned occasion=0. |
| `W_KAPPA_WEIGHT_VARIES_WITHIN_OCCASION` | warning | A weighted kappa's weight expression evaluates to different values (relative difference above `1e-9`) at two observation records of the same occasion, or of the same group of the kappa's level when nested levels are declared. κ is drawn once per occasion or group, so its effective variance Ω_IOV/W is ambiguous; each record is scaled by its own weight. |
| `W_LEVEL_SUMMARY` | info | Informational, not a finding, so reported with severity `info` and not counted as a warning (#2387): one row per level of a model with nested levels, outermost first, e.g. ``level `ARM`: 7 groups in 3 `STUDY` groups (per `STUDY` group: min 1, median 2, max 4); 1 of 3 `STUDY` groups holds a single `ARM` group; 1 kappa at `ARM` (K_ARM). |
| `W_MISSING_DV` | warning | One or more `EVID=0` rows had a missing `DV` (`.`/`NA`/blank) but were not marked `MDV=1`; they were skipped rather than scored as `DV=0`. |
| `W_MODELED_DURATION_NONPOSITIVE` | warning | For a `RATE=-2` dose into compartment `n`, the modeled duration `D{n}` evaluated at that dose's typical-value snapshot (initial θ, η = 0) is at or below `1e-8`. |
| `W_MODELED_RATE_NONPOSITIVE` | warning | For a `RATE=-1` dose into compartment `n`, the modeled rate `R{n}` evaluated at that dose's typical-value snapshot (initial θ, η = 0) is at or below `1e-8`. |
| `W_NEGATIVE_LAGTIME` | warning | `predict()` / `simulate()` only: the same finding as `E_NEGATIVE_LAGTIME`, on entry points that run no data errors. |
| `W_NN_WEIGHT_DIRECT_REFERENCE` | warning | An expression references a generated `[covariate_nn]` weight or bias θ directly rather than through the network's declared outputs. |
| `W_NO_DOSES` | warning | Zero dose events parsed across every subject, **although scored observations are present**. |
| `W_NO_FEASIBLE_EVAL` | warning | The outer optimizer finished without one feasible objective evaluation: every trial was rejected by the EBE convergence guard (`max_unconverged_frac`) or returned a non-finite objective. |
| `W_NONFINITE_OBJECTIVE` | warning | The objective at the final estimates is `NaN`, infinite, or at or above the `1e14` divergence cutoff, so the fit is demoted to `converged: false` whatever the optimizer's stop rule said; the message names which. |
| `W_ODE_SOLVER_DIAGNOSTICS` | warning | The ODE solver statistics of that pass (post-fit predictions at the final estimates, or the predict/simulate call at the supplied parameters) show an unclean integration. |
