| `W_ODE_SOLVER_ESCALATION_NOTE` | warning | Informational (severity `Info` in `warnings_structured`). `ode_method = auto` escalated one or more integration segments to a stiff stepper, and nothing else went wrong: no escalation was rejected, no step clamped at the minimum step size, no segment was unfinished. |
| `W_OUTPUT_DUPLICATE` | warning | A name in `[output]` is already written to sdtab automatically (e.g. `TAFD`, `TAD`, an eta name). |
| `W_PARSE` | warning | A warning the parser recorded while building the model that has no dedicated code. |
| `W_PER_CMT_UNMATCHED` | warning | The other direction of the two above: a compartment the model **declares** an entry for, that no observation is recorded on. |
| `W_RESIDUAL_CORRELATION_INERT` | warning | The model declares a serial residual `correlation` line, but in every subject each block formed by its `by` column(s) holds at most one observation. |
| `W_RESIDUAL_CORRELATION_PARTLY_CONFOUNDED_KAPPA` | warning | The same comparison holds in some subjects but not all, e.g. `cs by STUDY` next to a kappa at `ARM` where some studies have one arm. |
| `W_RTTE_DEGENERATE` | warning | While simulating a repeated-event (RTTE) stream, a subject's expected number of events before the horizon is non-finite or exceeds 1,000,000, so the stream is skipped; or a stream that passed that check produced more than 1,000,000 events, so it is truncated. |
| `W_SDE_LAGTIME` | warning | An absorption lag time on an SDE (`[diffusion]`) model is not honoured by the filter. |
| `W_SDE_RESET` | warning | EVID=3/4 resets under an SDE `[diffusion]` model are not honoured. |
| `W_SIMULATED_FLIP_FLOP` | warning | On a transit or inverse-Gaussian absorption closed form with no ODE twin, some simulated individuals with a positive dose before their last observation were evaluated at a sampled η inside the flip-flop regime (or the 2-cpt confluent-eigenvalue corner). |
| `W_STALLED_AT_INIT` | warning | The estimates never left the initial values. The test is the optimizer's own escape test when the result carries one (no packed coordinate moved by 1% of its scaled range), otherwise a comparison of the free θ, Ω and σ against their initial values at 1% relative. |
| `W_STEADY_STATE_ABSOLUTE_TIME` | warning | An `SS=1` dose (`II > 0`) on a model whose `[odes]` right-hand side reads an **absolute** clock — `TAFD`, `T`/`t`, or the bare `TIME` built-in. |
| `W_STEADY_STATE_II` | warning | SS=1 doses with missing / non-positive `II` (treated as non-SS). |
| `W_STEADY_STATE_INFUSION` | warning | SS=1 infusion whose length *after bioavailability* exceeds `II` (overlapping pulses; SS skipped) — the run-in's own test (#1281). |
| `W_STEADY_STATE_INIT` | warning | The model declares an `[initial_conditions]` baseline and at least one subject has a steady-state (`SS=1`) dose. |
| `W_TRANSIT_FLIP_FLOP` | warning | A transit absorption closed form (`one_cpt_transit` / `two_cpt_transit`) with an ODE twin has, at the initial typical values (η = 0) of at least one subject, a disposition rate (`CL/V`, or the 2-cpt fast rate α) at or above the transit rate `KTR = (n+1)/mtt`. ferx evaluates the equivalent `transit` ODE model for such parameters, which is correct but slower. |
| `W_TTE_DEGENERATE_HAZARD` | warning | While simulating a time-to-event endpoint with an analytic hazard, a subject drew a non-positive or non-finite effective hazard rate. |
| `W_UNCERTAINTY_DRAWS_SKIPPED` | warning | Some parameter draws of `simulate_with_uncertainty` put a transit or inverse-Gaussian closed form with no ODE twin into the flip-flop regime at typical values, where it has no solution, so those draws were not simulated. |
| `W_UNUSED_PARAM` | warning | A user-declared θ, ω or κ is not referenced by any `[individual_parameters]` or `[event_model]` expression, or a σ is not referenced in `[error_model]`. |
| `W_VI_BAD_BASIN` | warning | At the end of a `method = vi` run, the excess of the sampled data term over its value at the variational means is more than 25 times the `Σ dᵢ/2` a posterior-shaped `q` would give. |
| `W_VI_OMEGA_UNANCHORED` | warning | A method chain containing `vi` sets both `vi_kl = mc` and `vi_omega_update = adam`. |
| `W_ZERO_DV_MAGNITUDE_ONLY` | warning | Observations with `DV = 0` are scored by a residual error model whose variance is zero at a zero prediction: `proportional`, a `power(...)` magnitude, or a `combined` model whose additive SD starts at 0. |

## Fit object slots

Elements of the list `ferx_fit()` returns, for a fit of the warfarin example. Some slots are `NULL` unless the corresponding step or model feature is used. Descriptions are the first sentence of the entry in `?ferx_fit`, where it has one.

| Slot | Description |
|---|---|
| `aic` | Akaike Information Criterion |
| `bayes` |  |
| `bic` | Bayesian Information Criterion |
| `bic_inputs` | Named list of the free-parameter tally by Delattre class - n_obs, theta_random, theta_fixed, omega, kappa, sigma, sigma_random - which ferx_bic turns into the mixed / IIV / random BIC variants. |
| `bloq_method_label` | Character string describing the LOQ-censoring handling method used ("m3", "drop", etc.). |
| `call_settings` | Named list of the effective settings passed to Rust, with values typed back to their natural R types (logical, numeric, or character). |
| `cond_dist` |  |
| `condition_number` | Ratio of the largest to smallest eigenvalue of the correlation matrix of estimated parameters. |
| `converged` | Logical; did the optimizer converge |
| `cor_matrix` | Correlation matrix derived from cov_matrix, same dimnames. A correlation close to \pm 1 between two parameters flags a structural identifiability problem in the model. |
| `cov_fixed` | Logical vector, one entry per row of cov_matrix and named like them: TRUE for a coordinate the engine held rather than estimated - a parameter declared FIX, a theta the engine held because it had no effect on the objective (see theta_fixed), or a structural-zero covariance of a mixed block omega. |
| `cov_matrix` | Full parameter covariance matrix as a named numeric matrix (params × params). Row/column names use declared variable names ("TVCL", "ETA_CL", "EPS_PROP"); fallback is "OMEGA(1,1)" / "SIGMA(1)". |
| `covariance_method` | The estimator that produced cov_matrix and the standard errors: "r", "s" or "rsr", the [fit_options] token (ferx-core #1382). |
| `covariance_n_evals_estimated` | Estimated number of OFV calls required for the covariance step, computed before the step runs on large models. |
| `covariance_status` | String: "computed", "failed", "not_requested", or "sir_fallback" (the finite-difference Hessian was not positive definite and covariance_fallback = "sir" produced SIR-based intervals). |
| `covariance_wall_time_secs` | Wall-clock seconds spent in the covariance step. On a fresh fit it is part of wall_time_secs. 0 when the step did not run, or when the fit was loaded from a .fitrx bundle written before the field existed. |
| `covariate_names` | Character vector of non-standard column names present in the dataset (beyond ID, TIME, DV, EVID, AMT, CMT, RATE, MDV, II, SS, CENS, OCC). |
| `covariate_stats` | Data frame of the statistics a [covariate_model] relation stated symbolically (center = median, ref = mode, levels = auto) was resolved against: one row per covariate a relation reads, summarised over the fitted data (after [data_selection] and ignore). |
| `covariate_types` | Named character vector mapping each declared covariate to its type, "continuous" or "categorical" (the type from the [covariates] block). |
| `covtab` | Data frame echoing the declared covariate columns, present only when the model has a [covariates] block. |
| `data_hash` |  |
| `data_name` | Dataset name, derived as the basename of the data path with its extension stripped. |
| `data_path` |  |
| `dw_statistic` | Pooled Durbin-Watson statistic for IWRES within subjects. 2.0 = no autocorrelation; < 1.5 = positive autocorrelation (possible missing dynamics); > 2.5 = negative autocorrelation (possible over-parameterisation). |
| `ebe_convergence_warnings` | Number of outer iterations in which too many EBEs were unconverged (step was rejected by the guard). |
| `ebe_etas` | Data frame with one row per subject containing the BSV empirical Bayes estimates: ID plus one column per eta named after the model's eta declarations (e.g. ETA_CL, ETA_V). |
| `eigenvalues` | Numeric vector of eigenvalues of the correlation matrix of estimated (non-fixed) parameters, sorted descending. |
| `estimate_near_boundary` | TRUE when a theta is pinned to a declared bound - the predicate ferx_bootstrap applies as skip_estimate_near_boundary. |
| `estimates` | Tidy data frame of all estimated parameters (theta, omega diagonal, sigma, and - for IOV models - kappa diagonal), with columns param, transform, estimate, fixed, se, rse_pct, lower_95, upper_95, estimate_natural, lower_95_natural, upper_95_natural, init_as_sd, weight, scale, level. fixed is TRUE for a parameter the fit held (from theta_fixed / omega_fixed / sigma_fixed / kappa_fixed); its se, rse_pct and intervals are NA, since a held parameter has no standard error, and print() labels it NAME [FIX] with its SE as ---, as ferx-core's console does. |
| `eta_linked_theta` | Character vector parallel to eta_names: the typical-value theta each ETA is attached to, or "" when there is none or its statements disagree. |
| `eta_log_transformed` | Logical vector of length n_eta; TRUE when the eta is lognormally parameterised (THETA * exp(ETA)), FALSE for additive or unknown parameterisations. |
| `eta_names` | Character vector of ETA parameter names as declared in the model file (e.g. "ETA_CL", "ETA_V"). |
| `eta_normality` | Data frame with Shapiro-Wilk normality test for each ETA: columns eta, W, p_val, flag. |
| `eta_param_types` | Character vector parallel to eta_names: the scale each ETA enters its parameter on, "log_normal", "additive", "logit", "logit_probability" or "custom". |
| `exclusions` | Named list summarising records excluded by [data_selection] rules (model file and/or ignore/ accept/ignore_ids arguments). |
| `ferx_version` | ferx-core library version string. |
| `final_gradient` | Numeric vector containing the gradient of the objective function at the best-OFV parameter point (packed space: log-theta, Cholesky-omega, log-sigma). |
| `gradient` | The inner-loop gradient method as requested by the caller (usually "auto" or "fd"). |
| `gradient_method_inner` | Engine label for the inner-loop gradient method. Prefer gradient_used for display. |
| `gradient_method_outer` | Engine label for the population-level optimizer's gradient method. |
| `gradient_used` | The inner-loop gradient method the engine actually used: "analytic", "fd", or "N/A" (derivative-free / sampling step). |
| `imp_seed` | Numeric scalar (or NULL) giving the importance sampling seed. NULL when IS was not run. |
| `impmap_trace` |  |
| `importance_sampling` | Importance-sampling marginal log-likelihood diagnostics, populated only when the method chain ends with an "imp" stage (NULL otherwise). |
| `individual_estimates` | Data frame with one row per subject containing each subject's individual parameter values: ID plus one column per parameter declared in the [individual_parameters] block (e.g. CL, V, KA). |
| `inits_from_nca` | Character string giving the NCA initialisation method used ("nca", "nca_sweep", or "nca_ebe"), or NULL when model-file initial values were used directly. |
| `input_columns` | Includes both standard columns (ID, TIME, DV, etc.) and any covariate columns. Empty for in-memory fits that never read a file and absent after a ferx_save_fit/ferx_load_fit round-trip on older bundles. |
| `interaction` | Logical; the interaction flag the fitted objective ran under. TRUE for FOCEI and FALSE for FOCE; SAEM, VI and Gauss-Newton inherit it from the options they ran under. ferx_covariance() and ferx_sir() hand it back to the engine. |
| `iov_occasion` | Character string giving the IOV occasion rule the fit derived its occasions with, in the spelling settings = list(iov_occasion = ...) takes: "column", "dose" or "time(24, 48)". |
| `iwres_lag1_r` | Pooled lag-1 Pearson correlation of IWRES within subjects. Positive values indicate under-fitting, negative values indicate over-fitting. |
| `kappa_fixed` | Logical FIX flag per kappa, parallel to kappa_names; empty when the model has no IOV. |
| `kappa_init_as_sd` | Logical vector, one entry per IOV kappa parameter. Same semantics as omega_init_as_sd for inter-occasion variability. |
| `kappa_is_diagonal` | The same flag for the IOV (KAPPA) block; NA when the model declares no IOV. |
| `left_init` | The outer optimizer's own verdict on whether it left the initial estimates: TRUE, FALSE, or NA when the method recorded none. |
| `max_abs_correlation` | Largest absolute off-diagonal of the covariance matrix in correlation form, on the natural theta / OMEGA / SIGMA scale. |
| `max_unconverged_subjects` | Worst-case number of unconverged subjects in a single outer iteration. |
| `method` | Estimation method used |
| `method_chain` |  |
| `mixture_overrides` | Numeric vector: a [mixture] fit's fitted per-class overrides, one class variance per omega(k) override and then one class sigma per sigma(k) override, in declaration order (every estimator, SAEM included); NULL for a model without overrides. ferx_sir and ferx_covariance rebuild the per-class matrices from it. ferx_save_fit keeps it bit for bit; NULL on a fit loaded from a bundle saved before it was recorded. |
| `model_file_settings` | Named list of raw key = value pairs from the model file's [fit_options] block, as character strings (before Rust type coercion). |
| `model_hash` |  |
| `model_name` | Model name declared in the .ferx file by a top-level model \<name\> line (outside any [block], e.g. model warfarin_pk); the name is a single word. |
| `model_path` |  |
| `model_source` |  |
| `model_structure` | Named list returned by the Rust engine, derived from the parsed CompiledModel so it reflects exactly what ferx-core ran. |
| `model_text` | Verbatim content of the .ferx model file as a character string. NULL for in-memory fits that were never associated with a file, or for fits produced by older engine versions. |
| `multi_start_seed` | Numeric scalar (or NULL) giving the random seed used for multi-start parameter perturbation. |
| `n_iterations` | Number of outer iterations run |
| `n_obs` |  |
| `n_parameters` |  |
| `n_starts` | Integer. Number of multi-start runs attempted. 1 for single-start fits. |
| `n_subjects` |  |
| `n_threads_used` | Integer. Width of the worker pool the engine ran the fit on: the threads argument, else the model file's [fit_options] threads, else the engine default. |
| `neural_networks` | Named list of sub-lists, one per [covariate_nn] block declared in the model file. |
| `nlopt_missing_algorithms` | Character vector of NLopt algorithm names that are not available in the current build (empty on most platforms). |
| `obs_time_range` | Length-2 numeric vector c(min_time, max_time) across all observation records, or NULL when there are no observations. |
| `ode_linear_exact` | Logical; TRUE when the [odes] system was linear and solved exactly by the matrix exponential at the final estimates instead of integrated (ode_method = "auto" on a linear model, or ode_method = "linear"), with no segment falling back to integration. |
| `ofv` | Objective function value (-2 log-likelihood). The penalized objective when the model declares a prior(...) on any parameter, i.e. ofv_data + ofv_prior. |
| `ofv_data` | The data half of ofv - the -2 log-likelihood the AIC and BIC are computed from, and the value to compare against an unpriored fit of the same model. |
| `ofv_prior` | The prior half of ofv: the penalty summed over the priored coordinates. Exactly 0 when no prior is declared. |
| `omega` | Between-subject variability covariance matrix. Row and column names are the declared ETA names (e.g. "ETA_CL"); fallback is "OMEGA(1,1)" when names are absent. |
| `omega_fixed` | Logical FIX flags, one per theta, per eta (the omega diagonal; every eta of a fixed block is TRUE) and per sigma. |
| `omega_init` | Initial omega variance matrix, same layout as omega. A zero matrix for in-memory fits and older bundles. |
| `omega_init_as_sd` | Logical vector, one entry per BSV eta. TRUE when the corresponding omega line in the model file was annotated with (sd), meaning the initial value was specified as a standard deviation rather than a variance. print.ferx_fit() appends [initial specified as SD] to those rows. |
| `omega_init_dim` | Number of rows/columns of omega_init. |
| `omega_is_diagonal` | TRUE when the OMEGA block the fit was estimated under is diagonal, FALSE for a block_omega model, NA when the engine recorded no layout. |
| `optimizer_label` | Human-readable label for the outer optimizer used (e.g. "LBFGS", "BOBYQA"). Mirrors the optimizer enum value from ferx-core. |
| `outer_gtol` | Numeric. Gradient tolerance passed to the outer optimizer. |
| `outer_maxiter` | Integer. Maximum number of outer-loop iterations passed to the optimizer. |
| `packed_estimate` | Numeric vector: the optimizer's estimate on its packed scale (FOCE, FOCEI, Laplace and Gauss-Newton fits; NULL otherwise). ferx_covariance starts from it, which makes its result identical() to the inline covariance step. |
| `population_fingerprint` | Character strings holding the engine's JSON record of how the fit read its data (the model file's [data_selection] with ignore, accept, ignore_ids and settings = list(iov_column = ...) merged in) and a fingerprint of the population it read (about 270 bytes per subject). |
| `prior_summary` | Per-parameter prior report, or NULL when the model declares no prior. One row per priored parameter with columns name, prior_value, estimate, shift_in_prior_sds (signed, in prior SDs), penalty (this parameter's contribution to ofv_prior), family ("lognormal" or "normal", decided by the parameter's declared lower bound), and the implied 95% prior interval prior_lower_95 / prior_upper_95. |
| `profiled_blocks` | Character vector naming the level blocks declared theta NAMECOL, ... profile, in declaration order; character(0) for a fit without one. |
| `profiled_levels_at_bound` | Character vector of the theta names of the profiled levels that ended exactly on their block's declared bound (ferx-core #2112); character(0) when none did. |
| `reader_settings` | Character strings holding the engine's JSON record of how the fit read its data (the model file's [data_selection] with ignore, accept, ignore_ids and settings = list(iov_column = ...) merged in) and a fingerprint of the population it read (about 270 bytes per subject). |
| `saem_mu_ref_m_step_evals_saved` | Number of OFV evaluations saved by mu-referencing in the SAEM M-step. Only populated for SAEM fits with mu_referencing = TRUE; NULL otherwise. |
| `saem_n_subjects_hmc` | Integer count of subjects whose SAEM E-step proposals were generated by HMC (i.e. n_leapfrog > 0 and the AD build is active). |
| `saem_seed` | Numeric scalar (or NULL) giving the SAEM stochastic seed. NULL for non-SAEM methods. |
| `scoring_settings` | Named list of the inner-loop and ODE settings the stage that produced the estimates scored the objective under: inner_maxiter, inner_tol (as the stage ran it, after the tightening ferx applies for LTBS and quadrature), inner_restarts, inner_screen, inner_twin_seed, mu_referencing, n_agq, inner_optimizer, ebe_warm_start, ode_reltol, ode_abstol, ode_max_steps, ode_method, ode_stiff_abort_after (NA when off), ode_auto_switch, gradient_method (the gradient route the fit took, "auto" or "fd"), and nn_l2_lambda / nn_smooth_lambda (the [covariate_nn] penalty strengths the objective carried, ferx-core#1352; a recorded one is kept by ferx_covariance() whatever its arguments, NA when unrecorded), with the values [fit_options] spells. ferx_covariance scores under them, and ferx_save_fit keeps them. |
| `sdtab` | Data frame with ID, TIME, DV, PRED, IPRED, CWRES, IWRES, EBE_OFV, N_OBS; OCC if any subject carries an occasion column; CENS if any rows are LOQ-censored; CMT if the dataset has more than one endpoint (any observation with CMT != 1). |
| `se_omega` | Standard errors for omega elements. For diagonal omega, a vector of length n_eta (one per variance). |
| `se_sigma` | Standard errors for sigma (on the SD scale, like sigma itself) |
| `se_theta` | Standard errors for theta (NULL if covariance step failed) |
| `shrinkage_eps` | EPS shrinkage: 1 - SD(IWRES). NA when fewer than 2 valid residuals. |
| `shrinkage_eta` | Numeric vector of ETA shrinkage per random effect (1 - SD(eta_hat_k) / sqrt(omega_kk)). |
| `sigma` | Residual error parameter estimates on the standard-deviation scale. For a proportional component CV% = sigma * 100; for an additive component the value is in observation units. |
| `sigma_fixed` | Logical FIX flags, one per theta, per eta (the omega diagonal; every eta of a fixed block is TRUE) and per sigma. |
| `sigma_init` | Numeric vector of initial sigma values, parallel to sigma and sigma_names. |
| `sigma_init_as_sd` | Logical vector, one entry per sigma component. Same semantics as omega_init_as_sd for residual-error parameters. |
| `sigma_names` | Names of the sigma parameters as declared in the [parameters] block of the .ferx file. |
| `sigma_types` | Per-component error type label, parallel to sigma: "proportional" or "additive". |
| `sir_resamples` |  |
| `sir_resamples_dim` |  |
| `sir_resamples_n` |  |
| `sir_seed_used` | Numeric scalar giving the seed SIR resampled with: sir_seed, or the built-in default 12345 when sir_seed was unset. |
| `sir_settings` | Named list of the settings the fit's SIR ran under: samples, resamples, seed (resolved: 12345 when sir_seed was unset), df, scale, keep_samples, and scoring, the inner-loop and ODE settings each draw was scored with, shaped as scoring_settings. ferx_sir repeats this SIR by default and records its own run here; ferx_save_fit keeps it. |
| `stalled_at_init` | TRUE when no free parameter moved more than 1\% of its initial value, \code{NA} when the fit carries nothing to judge by. |
| `subject_ids` | Character vector of every subject's ID, verbatim from the data and in fit order (the rows of ebe_etas). |
| `subject_summary` | Data frame with one row per subject, in fit order (the entries of subject_ids): ID; ofv_contribution, the subject's contribution to the OFV; n_obs, its continuous (Gaussian) observations; and n_obs_discrete, its discrete (binary) observation records. sdtab holds each subject's n_obs rows in subject order, then each subject's n_obs_discrete rows in subject order. |
| `theta` | Named numeric vector of fixed effect estimates. A free level of a theta NAME[COL, ...] level block is named NAME[COL=value,...], e.g. PLACEBO[STUDY=1,TIME=4]. |
| `theta_fixed` | Logical FIX flags, one per theta, per eta (the omega diagonal; every eta of a fixed block is TRUE) and per sigma. |
| `theta_init` | Numeric vector of initial theta values as supplied to the optimizer, parallel to theta and theta_names. |
| `theta_levels` | Data frame with one row per level of each theta NAME[COL, ...] level block, as the block was bound to the fitted data (after [data_selection] and ignore), with columns block, index (1-based level position within the block), label (COL=value,...), group (contrast group, 0-based), contrast (the resolved convention: "sum_to_zero", "sum_to_zero_within", "ref" or "none"), profiled (TRUE on every level of a block declared profile: its levels were solved for at every outer step rather than searched by the optimizer, see profiled_blocks), theta_name (the level's name in theta, NA for a level the contrast derives from the others) and value (the level's fitted value, derived levels included: minus the sum of its group's free levels under sum_to_zero / sum_to_zero_within, 0 for a ref reference level. |
| `theta_transforms` |  |
| `total_ebe_fallbacks` | Total Nelder-Mead fallback invocations across all subjects and iterations. |
| `uses_ode_solver` | Logical; TRUE when the model has an [odes] block, FALSE for an analytical model. |
| `uses_sde` | Logical; TRUE when the model file contained a [diffusion] block and the fit used the Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) likelihood. |
| `wall_time_secs` | Total wall-clock time for the fit in seconds. |
| `warning_details` | List of the engine warnings that carry a structured details payload (ferx-core #2268), one named list per warning with severity, category, message, source_method (when set) and details - for example the full unusable_subjects list of W_NONFINITE_OBJECTIVE, whose message names at most ten. ferx_save_fit keeps it, in the .fitrx slot ferx-core writes, and ferx_get_warnings(as_df = TRUE) shows each payload beside its warning. |
| `warnings` | Character vector of warnings |
| `warnings_category` |  |
| `warnings_message` |  |
| `warnings_severity` |  |
| `warnings_source_method` |  |
| `warnings_structured` | Data frame with columns severity ("critical", "warning", or "info"), category (a fixed vocabulary such as "convergence", "covariance_step", "dw_autocorrelation"), message, and source_method (the estimation stage that emitted the warning, e.g. "FOCEI"; empty string when not applicable). |

## Not available from R

Features documented for ferx-core that the pinned ferx-r build cannot run, or runs only partly:

| Feature | Status at the pinned build | Where to look |
|---|---|---|
| Variational inference as `ferx_fit(method = "vi")` | The `method` argument rejects it; `method = vi` in `[fit_options]` runs | @sec-estimation-methods |
| `[markov_model]` (continuous-time Markov endpoints) | Rejected at parse time: ferx-r does not build the engine's `markov` feature | [Markov models](https://ferx-nlme.org/ferx-core/model-file/markov-model.html) |
| `[simulation]` block | Read by the ferx-core command line only; ferx-r's simulation functions need a dataset | @sec-simulation |
| `[dynamics_nn]` (neural-network ODE terms) | Not implemented (design only) | [Neural networks](https://ferx-nlme.org/ferx-core/model-file/neural-networks.html) |
| Hand-written `[covariate_model]` relations, repeated time-to-event, fixed-rate infusions into the central compartment | Fit from R, but no bundled ferx-r example | @sec-covariates, @sec-time-to-event, @sec-dosing |
| `[mixture]` models, modelled infusion rate or duration (`RATE = -1`, `-2`) | No bundled example | @sec-variability, [data format](https://ferx-nlme.org/ferx-core/data-format.html) |
| VI's ELBO and per-subject posterior summaries | Not on the R fit object | [Variational inference](https://ferx-nlme.org/ferx-core/estimation/vi.html) |

## Feature maturity

The maturity label of each ferx-core feature at the pinned engine (ferx-core {{< var ferx_core_sha_short >}}). **stable** features are well tested across datasets and estimation options; **beta** features are stable in limited testing; **experimental** features have been tested on a few examples and may change. See the ferx-core [feature maturity](https://ferx-nlme.org/ferx-core/maturity.html) page.

| Feature | Maturity | ferx-core page |
|---|---|---|
| Parameters (theta / omega / sigma, block omega) | stable | [Parameters](https://ferx-nlme.org/ferx-core/model-file/parameters.html) |
| Inter-occasion variability (IOV) | stable | [IOV](https://ferx-nlme.org/ferx-core/model-file/iov.html) |
| Covariates | stable | [Covariates](https://ferx-nlme.org/ferx-core/model-file/covariates.html) |
| Structural model — analytical PK (1/2/3-cpt) | stable | [Structural Model](https://ferx-nlme.org/ferx-core/model-file/structural-model.html) |
| Lag time | stable | [Lagtime](https://ferx-nlme.org/ferx-core/model-file/lagtime.html) |
